Part 12 — Production Usage

Views in Production

Banking — Customer 360 Read Model

sql
-- Flyway: src/main/resources/db/migration/V12__customer_360_view.sql
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW v_customer_360 AS
SELECT
    c.customer_id,
    c.email,
    c.region,
    c.status AS customer_status,
    COALESCE(SUM(a.balance) FILTER (WHERE a.status = 'ACTIVE'), 0) AS active_balance,
    COUNT(a.account_id) FILTER (WHERE a.status = 'ACTIVE') AS active_accounts,
    MAX(t.created_at) AS last_transaction_at
FROM customers c
LEFT JOIN accounts a ON a.customer_id = c.customer_id
LEFT JOIN transactions t ON t.account_id = a.account_id
GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.email, c.region, c.status;

-- Grant to reporting role only
-- GRANT SELECT ON v_customer_360 TO reporting_role;

FROM accounts a

❌ View on hot path replacing 2-line indexed query — extra indirection, no benefit

✅ Encapsulate window/CTE logic reused by 5+ consumers

Part 14 — Hibernate/JPA Integration

ORM and Views

@Subselect vs @Table on View

java
// Option A: @Subselect — Hibernate generates SELECT from entity
@Entity
@Immutable
@Subselect("SELECT customer_id, email, total_balance FROM v_active_customer_balances")
public class ActiveCustomerBalanceView { ... }

// Option B: @Table(name = "v_customer_360") — view as "table"
@Entity
@Immutable
@Table(name = "v_customer_360")
public class Customer360View { ... }

// Both read-only — never @Entity write operations on views without INSTEAD OF

@Synchronize — Cache Invalidation Hint

java
@Subselect("SELECT * FROM v_customer_360")
@Synchronize({"customers", "accounts", "transactions"})
// Tells Hibernate: changes to these tables may invalidate query cache for this entity

What Not to Do

java
// ❌ @Entity on view with @OneToMany to base entities — mapping nightmare
// ❌ save() on view entity — fails or undefined
// ❌ ddl-auto: update creating "view" as table — disable ddl-auto in prod

// ✅ Read-only DTO projection layer
// ✅ Separate package: ...domain.view.readonly

Native Query Alternative

public interface Customer360Projection {
    Long getCustomerId();
    String getEmail();
    BigDecimal getActiveBalance();
}

@Query(value = "SELECT * FROM v_customer_360 WHERE region = :region", nativeQuery = true)
List<Customer360Projection> byRegion(@Param("region") String region);

Mistake 1: View for Performance Without Materialization

-- Flyway replaces view, renames total_balance → balance_total

Part 19 — Interview Questions

Junior

Q1: What is a database view?

A named stored SELECT query that acts like a virtual table — no separate stored data for standard views.

Q2: View vs table?

Table stores data physically; view stores definition and computes results from base tables at query time.

Q3: Can you INSERT into a view?

Sometimes — if view is simple (single table, no aggregation). Complex views need INSTEAD OF triggers or are read-only.

Q4: View vs CTE?

View is permanent catalog object, reusable and permissioned. CTE is statement-scoped.

Q5: Does a view improve query performance?

Not by itself — same as running underlying SQL unless materialized.

Mid-Level

Q6: What is view merging?

Optimizer expands view into outer query and optimizes as one statement — predicate pushdown possible.

Q7: WITH CHECK OPTION purpose?

Prevents DML through view that would make row invisible to view — maintains consistency.

Q8: How would you expose latest payment per customer to multiple apps?

Create view with ROW_NUMBER pattern (or materialized view if heavy); GRANT SELECT; map read-only entity.

Q9: How to secure columns with views?

View selecting subset of columns; GRANT on view only; app role has no base table access.

Q10: DROP TABLE CASCADE impact on views?

Dependent views dropped — migration ordering critical in Flyway.

Senior

Q11: When use INSTEAD OF trigger on view?

Complex view must accept writes — trigger decomposes to base table DML. Prefer writing base tables directly when possible.

Q12: View on read replica for reporting — pitfalls?

Replication lag — stale reads; long-running view query load on replica not primary — good; monitor replica lag for finance reports.

Q13: Hibernate @Subselect vs @Table on view?

@Subselect embeds SQL in mapping; @Table maps to view name. Both @Immutable for read-only.

Q14: Non-mergeable view symptoms?

Subquery scan block in EXPLAIN; outer filters not pushed; fix by simplifying view or using materialized view.

Staff / Architect

Q15: Microservice A needs Customer data owned by Service B — view?

No cross-DB view. API, event replication, or dedicated read model populated by Kafka.

Q16: Enterprise view governance?

Catalog, owners, consumers, index deps, breaking change policy, quarterly review, no view stacks >2 deep without justification.

Scenario

Scenario: "Dashboard querying v_daily_payment_summary times out."

EXPLAIN — full scan payments 2 years + group. Add index (created_at, region) on payments; narrow view date range; move to materialized view refreshed hourly; route to replica; pre-aggregate in batch table.

Part 1 — Concept

What Is a Stored Procedure?

A stored procedure is a named block of procedural SQL (and sometimes procedural language code) stored in the database catalog. It is invoked with CALL (or EXEC) and can accept parameters, run multiple statements, use control flow (IF/LOOP), and define its own transaction boundaries.

sql
-- PostgreSQL example
CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE sp_transfer_funds(
    p_from_account_id BIGINT,
    p_to_account_id   BIGINT,
    p_amount          NUMERIC(18,2),
    INOUT p_transfer_id BIGINT DEFAULT NULL
)
LANGUAGE plpgsql
AS $$
BEGIN
    IF p_amount <= 0 THEN
        RAISE EXCEPTION 'Amount must be positive';
    END IF;

    UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance - p_amount
    WHERE account_id = p_from_account_id AND status = 'ACTIVE';

    IF NOT FOUND THEN
        RAISE EXCEPTION 'Source account invalid or inactive';
    END IF;

    UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance + p_amount
    WHERE account_id = p_to_account_id AND status = 'ACTIVE';

    IF NOT FOUND THEN
        RAISE EXCEPTION 'Destination account invalid or inactive';
    END IF;

    INSERT INTO transfers (from_account_id, to_account_id, amount, created_at)
    VALUES (p_from_account_id, p_to_account_id, p_amount, NOW())
    RETURNING transfer_id INTO p_transfer_id;
END;
$$;

-- Invoke
CALL sp_transfer_funds(5001, 5002, 2500.00, NULL);

Stored Procedure vs Other Database Objects

text
┌──────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Object           │ Purpose                                            │
├──────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ VIEW (L20)       │ Named SELECT — virtual table, no procedural logic  │
│ FUNCTION (L22)   │ Returns value; often used in SELECT expressions    │
│ STORED PROCEDURE │ Side effects + control flow; CALL/EXEC             │
│ TRIGGER (L23)    │ Fires automatically on DML events                  │
│ Plain SQL        │ Ad hoc or app-embedded; no catalog persistence     │
└──────────────────┴────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Procedure Classification

text
STORED PROCEDURES

├── By parameter mode
│   ├── IN       → input only (default)
│   ├── OUT      → output only
│   └── INOUT    → input + returned to caller
│
├── By language
│   ├── SQL procedural (PL/SQL, PL/pgSQL, T-SQL)
│   └── External (Java in Oracle, C in PostgreSQL — rare)
│
├── By transaction behavior
│   ├── Runs in caller's transaction (default many DBs)
│   ├── COMMIT/ROLLBACK inside (Oracle autonomous, PG procedures PG11+)
│   └── Nested savepoints
│
├── By purpose
│   ├── Business workflow (transfer, settlement batch)
│   ├── ETL / batch maintenance
│   ├── Admin / migration utilities
│   └── Legacy encapsulation (thick DB era)
│
└── By exposure
    ├── Application API (called from Spring)
    ├── Scheduled DBA jobs
    └── Internal (called only by other procedures)

ASCII — Call Flow

text
Spring Boot Service                    Database
┌─────────────────────┐               ┌──────────────────────────────┐
│ @Transactional      │   CALL        │ sp_transfer_funds            │
│ transferService     │ ──────────►   │  ├─ validate amount          │
│                     │               │  ├─ UPDATE accounts (debit)  │
│ SimpleJdbcCall /    │   OUT params  │  ├─ UPDATE accounts (credit) │
│ EntityManager       │ ◄──────────   │  ├─ INSERT transfers         │
└─────────────────────┘               │  └─ COMMIT or ROLLBACK       │
                                      └──────────────────────────────┘

Part 2 — History

Evolution of Stored Procedures

text
1980s   Oracle PL/SQL — stored procedures as application server inside DB
        Sybase T-SQL procedures — financial systems batch processing
        "Thick database" architecture: business rules in Oracle packages

1990s   SQL:1999 adds CALL statement for procedures
        Microsoft SQL Server stored procs dominate enterprise .NET stacks
        DB2 SQL procedures; banking cores on mainframe + DB2 procs

2000s   Java EE / Spring rise — "thin database, thick application"
        Hibernate ORM — CRUD in Java; procs for reporting/batch only
        Stored procs criticized: vendor lock-in, untestable, hidden logic

2010s   Microservices — strong preference for logic in services
        Flyway/Liquibase version proc DDL like application code
        PostgreSQL 11 (2018) — true PROCEDURE with COMMIT support

2020s   Pragmatic split:
        - Domain logic → Spring Boot services
        - Atomic multi-step DB workflows → procedures (sometimes)
        - Batch ETL, partition maintenance → procedures
        - Legacy Oracle/DB2 estates — massive proc inventory remains

Historical Lesson

Stored procedures were the original microservice — logic colocated with data for network efficiency on mainframes. Today, default architecture puts business rules in application services; procedures remain for atomicity at data layer, batch jobs, and legacy integration. A Solution Architect must know when proc-heavy design is debt vs deliberate boundary.

Part 3 — Problem Statement

What Problems Do Stored Procedures Solve?

Problem 1: Multi-Statement Atomic Workflow at DB Boundary

sql
-- Transfer: debit + credit + audit log must succeed or fail together
-- One round trip; locks held consistently; no partial state between app statements
CALL sp_transfer_funds(5001, 5002, 1000.00, NULL);

Problem 2: Reduce Network Round Trips (Legacy / Batch)

sql
-- Process 10,000 end-of-day interest accruals in one CALL
CALL sp_accrue_daily_interest(p_business_date => CURRENT_DATE);
-- Loop inside procedure — one network hop vs 10,000 UPDATE statements from app

Problem 3: Consistent Rules Across Multiple Consumers

sql
-- BI tool, batch job, and Java app all CALL same settlement proc
-- Single definition of settlement logic (when org standardizes on DB layer)
CALL sp_settle_payment_batch(p_batch_id => 98765);

Problem 4: Security — Expose Operations Not Tables

sql
-- App role: EXECUTE on sp_create_payment, no direct INSERT on payments
GRANT EXECUTE ON PROCEDURE sp_create_payment TO payment_app_role;
-- REVOKE INSERT ON payments FROM payment_app_role;

Problem 5: Complex Batch / Maintenance

sql
-- Partition rotation, archive purge, statistics refresh
CALL sp_archive_transactions(p_older_than => CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '7 years');

Unified Problem Statement

Stored procedures bundle multi-step database work into a single invocable unit with parameters, control flow, and transaction control — reducing round trips and colocating atomic DB workflows with the data they modify.

Part 4 — Why This Exists

Why Procedures vs Application Code?

Original Drivers (Still Valid in Niches)

text
1. Network latency — one CALL vs many JDBC round trips
2. Lock consistency — debit/credit in one transaction without interleaving
3. Permission model — GRANT EXECUTE without table DML rights
4. Batch performance — set-oriented loops close to data

Why Spring Boot Usually Owns Business Logic Today

text
✅ Unit tests with JUnit/Mockito — fast CI
✅ Version control + code review culture in Java teams
✅ Portable across databases (mostly)
✅ Observability — logs, traces, metrics in app layer
✅ Domain model — entities, events, Kafka integration
✅ Team skills — Java developers, not PL/SQL specialists

When Procedures Still Win

ScenarioProcedureApplication
Simple CRUD❌✅ JPA
Transfer debit+credit+ledgerEither — often app @Transactional✅ default
10M row nightly batch on DB✅❌ pulling rows to app
Oracle legacy package (10 years)✅ maintain❌ rewrite cost
Cross-service orchestration❌✅ Saga in services
Hide table from app role✅ EXECUTE grantPartial (API only)

Architect Principle

text
Default: business rules in Spring Boot + @Transactional
Exception: batch/maintenance, legacy, or proven hot-path atomic DB workflow
Never: procedures that CALL external HTTP or hide domain logic nobody can test

Part 5 — Internal Working

How Stored Procedures Execute Internally

Catalog Storage

text
System catalogs store:
  - Procedure name, schema, owner
  - Parameter names, types, IN/OUT/INOUT modes
  - Source code or compiled bytecode (Oracle PL/SQL compiled)
  - Language (plpgsql, sql, plsql, tsql)
  - Dependencies on tables, types, other procs
  - Security: SECURITY INVOKER vs DEFINER (PostgreSQL)

Parse and Plan

text
First CALL after CREATE:
  Parse procedure body
  Compile to internal representation (PostgreSQL: function/procedure tree)
  Cache in plan cache / shared pool (Oracle)

Subsequent CALLs:
  Reuse cached plan for procedure body
  Embedded SQL statements inside proc may get individual plans (prepared)

Dynamic SQL (EXECUTE IMMEDIATE):
  Re-parse each execution — plan instability

Execution Model

text
CALL sp_transfer_funds(5001, 5002, 1000, NULL):

1. Resolve procedure in catalog
2. Bind IN parameters (5001, 5002, 1000)
3. Begin transaction (if not already in caller txn — DB-specific)
4. Execute body sequentially:
     - IF checks
     - UPDATE accounts ... (row locks acquired)
     - INSERT transfers ...
5. Set OUT/INOUT parameters
6. COMMIT (if proc commits) or return to caller txn
7. Return control to JDBC CallableStatement

Transaction Semantics by Database

text
PostgreSQL PROCEDURE (11+):
  Can COMMIT/ROLLBACK inside procedure
  CALL runs in transaction context

Oracle PL/SQL:
  Default: part of caller session transaction
  AUTONOMOUS TRANSACTION pragma: separate commit (logging)

SQL Server:
  EXEC proc — same transaction unless nested with @@TRANCOUNT
  TRY/CATCH + ROLLBACK patterns

MySQL:
  PROCEDURE — no COMMIT inside until recent versions; mostly caller txn

SECURITY DEFINER (PostgreSQL)

sql
CREATE PROCEDURE sp_admin_purge(...)
LANGUAGE plpgsql
SECURITY DEFINER  -- runs with owner's privileges, not caller's
AS $$ ... $$;
-- Elevated privilege pattern — use carefully; search_path attacks possible

Part 6 — Storage Internals

Procedures and Storage

Procedure Body — Catalog Only

text
Source text stored in:
  PostgreSQL: pg_proc.prosrc
  Oracle: ALL_SOURCE
  SQL Server: sys.sql_modules

Disk: kilobytes per procedure — negligible
Not data storage — unlike materialized views

Data Modified by Procedure

text
Procedure UPDATE/INSERT affects base table storage:
  Heap pages, indexes, WAL/redo logs
  Same as equivalent statements from application

Batch proc updating 1M rows:
  Same I/O as 1M row update from JDBC batch
  Advantage: no network transfer of rows to app — stays in DB engine

Temp Storage Inside Procedure

sql
-- Internal temp tables, cursor results, sort spills
CREATE PROCEDURE sp_report AS
BEGIN
    CREATE TEMP TABLE tmp_results AS SELECT ...;  -- session temp
    -- temp files if large sort
END;

WAL / Redo Volume

text
Transfer proc: 2 UPDATEs + 1 INSERT = 3 WAL records (simplified)
Same as 3 JDBC statements in one @Transactional — identical durability story
Procedure does NOT reduce WAL — reduces round trips only

Part 7 — Memory Usage

Procedure Memory Impact

ComponentMemory
Procedure cacheShared pool — compiled body
Session variablesStack — small
Cursor FOR loopPer-row or set fetch — work_mem for sorts
Temp tables in procSession temp — temp buffers
Bulk COLLECT (Oracle)PGA — can OOM if unbounded
JDBC CallableStatementClient heap — parameter binding

Oracle PGA Warning

sql
-- ❌ Unbounded collection in PL/SQL
SELECT bulk collect INTO arr FROM transactions;  -- 50M rows → PGA explosion

-- ✅ Set-based SQL or LIMIT/batch loop with COMMIT in batch job

PostgreSQL work_mem

text
Procedure running heavy SELECT ... GROUP BY inside:
  Same work_mem per sort/hash node as standalone query
  Batch jobs: SET LOCAL work_mem = '256MB' at start of CALL

Connection Hold Time

text
Long-running procedure holds JDBC connection from pool
Spring: increase timeout; dedicated batch pool
Risk: connection pool exhaustion during sp_nightly_settlement

Part 8 — Execution Flow

Stored Procedure Execution Flows

Flow 1: Simple IN Parameters — Payment Creation

sql
CREATE PROCEDURE sp_create_payment(
    IN p_customer_id BIGINT,
    IN p_amount NUMERIC(18,2),
    IN p_client_request_id VARCHAR(64),
    OUT p_payment_id BIGINT
)
-- body: idempotency check, INSERT, set OUT
text
1. Spring opens connection, begins @Transactional
2. CallableStatement: {call sp_create_payment(?, ?, ?, ?)}
3. Bind IN params; register OUT parameter
4. DB executes: SELECT EXISTS idempotency → INSERT payments → set p_payment_id
5. Spring commits transaction
6. Read OUT parameter → return to caller

Flow 2: Transfer with Exception Rollback

text
1. CALL sp_transfer_funds(...)
2. Debit account 5001 — OK, row lock held
3. Credit account 5002 — insufficient privilege / inactive → RAISE EXCEPTION
4. PostgreSQL: entire transaction aborted (unless SAVEPOINT used)
5. Spring: catch DataAccessException, translate to TransferFailedException
6. No partial transfer — atomicity preserved

Flow 3: Batch Procedure with Internal COMMIT (PostgreSQL)

sql
CREATE PROCEDURE sp_archive_old_txn(p_cutoff DATE)
LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
DECLARE
    batch_size INT := 10000;
BEGIN
    LOOP
        WITH moved AS (
            DELETE FROM transactions WHERE created_at < p_cutoff LIMIT batch_size
            RETURNING *
        )
        INSERT INTO transactions_archive SELECT * FROM moved;

        COMMIT;  -- PG procedure: commit batch, release locks
        EXIT WHEN NOT FOUND;  -- simplified
    END LOOP;
END;
$$;
text
Each COMMIT: sub-transaction completes, WAL flushed
Failure mid-batch: earlier batches committed — partial progress (by design for batch)
App must track progress or use idempotent batches

Flow 4: Security DEFINER Procedure

text
1. App role (limited) CALL sp_sensitive_read(...)
2. Procedure runs as owner (DBA-defined definer)
3. Internal SELECT on restricted table — allowed via definer rights
4. Returns filtered result to caller
5. Audit: log caller identity inside proc (session_user)

Flow 5: Procedure Calling Procedure

sql
CALL sp_end_of_day();
  → CALL sp_accrue_interest();
  → CALL sp_generate_statements();
  → CALL sp_notify_settlement();  -- may only enqueue DB table, not HTTP
text
Nested call stack in DB session
Single transaction unless inner proc COMMITs (PostgreSQL batch pattern)
Oracle packages: grouped related procedures — namespace organization

Part 9 — Performance Analysis

Stored Procedure Performance

What Procedures Improve

text
✅ Network round trips: 1 CALL vs N statements
✅ Payload: no shipping intermediate result sets to app and back
✅ Parse once: cached procedure body
✅ Batch loops on server — set operations stay in engine

What Procedures Do NOT Improve

text
❌ WAL volume for same DML
❌ Missing indexes on tables
❌ Row-by-row loop in PL/SQL vs set-based SQL (often slower than one UPDATE)
❌ Hiding N+1 cursor loop inside proc — still N+1 in DB

Set-Based vs Row-by-Row in Procedures

sql
-- ❌ Slow — cursor loop
FOR rec IN SELECT account_id FROM accounts LOOP
    UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance * 1.001 WHERE account_id = rec.account_id;
END LOOP;

-- ✅ Fast — single statement
UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance * 1.001 WHERE status = 'ACTIVE';

Performance Hierarchy

text
FAST:
  One set-based SQL statement in proc (or skip proc — use app @Transactional)
  Batch DELETE/INSERT with LIMIT batches + COMMIT for lock duration control

SLOW:
  Row-by-row procedural loop on millions of rows
  Dynamic SQL without bind variables — hard parse each time
  Long proc holding locks — blocks OLTP

MEASURE:
  EXPLAIN ANALYZE on SQL inside proc
  pg_stat_statements / Oracle AWR for proc execution stats

Part 10 — Complexity Analysis

PatternTimeNotes
Proc with k set-based DMLO(sum of DML costs)Same as k JDBC calls
Row loop n iterationsO(n × per-row cost)Often bad
Batch archive b rows/batchO(total/b × commit cost)Tunable
Network savedO(1) round trip vs O(k)Main proc benefit
Parse cache hitO(1) compileFirst call O(parse)

Part 11 — Code / SQL Examples

Stored Procedure Masterclass

PostgreSQL — Idempotent Payment

sql
CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE sp_create_payment(
    IN  p_customer_id       BIGINT,
    IN  p_amount            NUMERIC(18,2),
    IN  p_client_request_id VARCHAR(64),
    OUT p_payment_id        BIGINT,
    OUT p_status            VARCHAR(20)
)
LANGUAGE plpgsql
AS $$
BEGIN
    SELECT payment_id, status
    INTO p_payment_id, p_status
    FROM payments
    WHERE client_request_id = p_client_request_id;

    IF FOUND THEN
        RETURN;  -- idempotent — already exists
    END IF;

    INSERT INTO payments (customer_id, amount, client_request_id, status, created_at)
    VALUES (p_customer_id, p_amount, p_client_request_id, 'PENDING', NOW())
    RETURNING payment_id INTO p_payment_id;

    p_status := 'PENDING';
END;
$$;

PostgreSQL — Transfer with Savepoint

sql
CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE sp_transfer_funds(
    IN p_from BIGINT, IN p_to BIGINT, IN p_amount NUMERIC(18,2)
)
LANGUAGE plpgsql
AS $$
DECLARE
    v_from_bal NUMERIC(18,2);
BEGIN
    IF p_amount <= 0 THEN
        RAISE EXCEPTION 'INVALID_AMOUNT';
    END IF;

    SELECT balance INTO v_from_bal
    FROM accounts WHERE account_id = p_from AND status = 'ACTIVE'
    FOR UPDATE;

    IF v_from_bal IS NULL THEN
        RAISE EXCEPTION 'SOURCE_NOT_FOUND';
    END IF;

    IF v_from_bal < p_amount THEN
        RAISE EXCEPTION 'INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS';
    END IF;

    UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance - p_amount WHERE account_id = p_from;
    UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance + p_amount WHERE account_id = p_to;

    INSERT INTO transfers (from_account_id, to_account_id, amount, created_at)
    VALUES (p_from, p_to, p_amount, NOW());
END;
$$;

Oracle PL/SQL — Package Pattern

sql
CREATE OR REPLACE PACKAGE pkg_payments AS
    PROCEDURE create_payment(
        p_customer_id IN NUMBER,
        p_amount      IN NUMBER,
        p_request_id  IN VARCHAR2,
        p_payment_id  OUT NUMBER
    );
    PROCEDURE settle_batch(p_batch_id IN NUMBER);
END pkg_payments;
/

CREATE OR REPLACE PACKAGE BODY pkg_payments AS
    PROCEDURE create_payment(...) IS
    BEGIN
        -- idempotency + insert
        NULL;
    END;
END pkg_payments;
/

-- Call
BEGIN
    pkg_payments.create_payment(1001, 500, 'req-abc', :payment_id);
END;
/

SQL Server — T-SQL with TRY/CATCH

sql
CREATE PROCEDURE dbo.sp_transfer_funds
    @from_account_id BIGINT,
    @to_account_id   BIGINT,
    @amount          DECIMAL(18,2)
AS
BEGIN
    SET NOCOUNT ON;
    BEGIN TRY
        BEGIN TRANSACTION;

        UPDATE dbo.accounts SET balance = balance - @amount
        WHERE account_id = @from_account_id AND balance >= @amount;

        IF @@ROWCOUNT = 0
            THROW 50001, 'Insufficient funds or account not found', 1;

        UPDATE dbo.accounts SET balance = balance + @amount
        WHERE account_id = @to_account_id;

        INSERT INTO dbo.transfers (from_account_id, to_account_id, amount)
        VALUES (@from_account_id, @to_account_id, @amount);

        COMMIT TRANSACTION;
    END TRY
    BEGIN CATCH
        IF @@TRANCOUNT > 0 ROLLBACK TRANSACTION;
        THROW;
    END CATCH
END;

DB2 — SQL Procedure

sql
CREATE PROCEDURE sp_close_account(IN p_account_id BIGINT)
LANGUAGE SQL
BEGIN
    DECLARE v_balance DECIMAL(18,2);

    SELECT balance INTO v_balance FROM accounts WHERE account_id = p_account_id;

    IF v_balance <> 0 THEN
        SIGNAL SQLSTATE '45000' SET MESSAGE_TEXT = 'Non-zero balance';
    END IF;

    UPDATE accounts SET status = 'CLOSED', closed_at = CURRENT TIMESTAMP
    WHERE account_id = p_account_id;
END;

Batch — Archive with Batched COMMIT (PostgreSQL)

sql
CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE sp_archive_transactions_batch(
    IN p_cutoff DATE,
    IN p_batch_size INT DEFAULT 5000
)
LANGUAGE plpgsql
AS $$
DECLARE
    v_deleted INT;
BEGIN
    LOOP
        WITH del AS (
            DELETE FROM transactions
            WHERE ctid IN (
                SELECT ctid FROM transactions
                WHERE created_at < p_cutoff
                LIMIT p_batch_size
            )
            RETURNING *
        )
        INSERT INTO transactions_archive SELECT * FROM del;

        GET DIAGNOSTICS v_deleted = ROW_COUNT;
        COMMIT;

        EXIT WHEN v_deleted = 0;
    END LOOP;
END;
$$;

Part 12 — Production Usage

Stored Procedures in Production

Banking — When Procs Remain Common

text
Legacy Oracle/DB2 cores:
  Interest calculation, GL posting, end-of-day settlement
  Package pkg_eod run by scheduler — decades of investment

Modern greenfield Spring Boot:
  @Transactional transferService.debitCredit() — NOT stored proc
  Exception: regulatory audit requires DB-side immutable posting pipeline

Payments — Idempotent Insert at DB (Debatable)

sql
-- Some teams use proc for idempotency + INSERT under EXECUTE-only role
CALL sp_create_payment(1001, 250.00, 'client-req-uuid-123', NULL, NULL);
-- Alternative (preferred modern): UNIQUE(client_request_id) + app retry

Nightly Batch on Read/Write Primary or Batch Node

text
Cron / K8s CronJob:
  psql -c "CALL sp_accrue_daily_interest(CURRENT_DATE)"
Dedicated connection pool; statement_timeout = 2h
Monitor: rows processed, duration, lock waits

Anti-Patterns in Production

text
❌ 5000-line Oracle package as entire business layer
❌ Procedure calling external systems (UTL_HTTP) — fragile, untestable
❌ Duplicate logic: proc + Java service diverge over time
❌ Flyway proc change without integration test against real DB
❌ COMMIT inside proc called from Spring @Transactional — txn boundary surprise

Operational Checklist

text
□ Version procs in Flyway/Liquibase (order before/after table migrations)
□ Integration tests with Testcontainers calling CallableStatement
□ Document IN/OUT params and error codes
□ Grant EXECUTE to app role only — not DBA owner in prod
□ pg_stat_user_functions / Oracle DBA_PROC_STATS monitoring
□ Rollback plan: CREATE OR REPLACE previous version in Flyway undo script

Part 13 — Spring Boot Integration

Calling Procedures from Spring Boot

SimpleJdbcCall (Recommended for Procedures)

java
@Service
@RequiredArgsConstructor
public class PaymentProcedureService {

    private final JdbcTemplate jdbcTemplate;

    public PaymentResult createPayment(CreatePaymentCommand cmd) {
        SimpleJdbcCall call = new SimpleJdbcCall(jdbcTemplate)
            .withProcedureName("sp_create_payment")
            .declareParameters(
                new SqlParameter("p_customer_id", Types.BIGINT),
                new SqlParameter("p_amount", Types.DECIMAL),
                new SqlParameter("p_client_request_id", Types.VARCHAR),
                new SqlOutParameter("p_payment_id", Types.BIGINT),
                new SqlOutParameter("p_status", Types.VARCHAR));

        Map<String, Object> in = Map.of(
            "p_customer_id", cmd.customerId(),
            "p_amount", cmd.amount(),
            "p_client_request_id", cmd.clientRequestId());

        Map<String, Object> out = call.execute(in);

        return new PaymentResult(
            (Long) out.get("p_payment_id"),
            (String) out.get("p_status"));
    }
}

CallableStatement — Explicit

java
@Transactional
public void transferFunds(long from, long to, BigDecimal amount) {
    jdbcTemplate.execute((Connection conn) -> {
        try (CallableStatement cs = conn.prepareCall(
                "{call sp_transfer_funds(?, ?, ?)}")) {
            cs.setLong(1, from);
            cs.setLong(2, to);
            cs.setBigDecimal(3, amount);
            cs.execute();
        }
        return null;
    });
}

Prefer @Transactional Service (Modern Default)

java
@Service
@RequiredArgsConstructor
public class TransferService {

    private final AccountRepository accountRepo;
    private final TransferRepository transferRepo;

    @Transactional
    public void transfer(TransferCommand cmd) {
        Account from = accountRepo.findByIdForUpdate(cmd.fromId())
            .orElseThrow(() -> new AccountNotFoundException(cmd.fromId()));
        Account to = accountRepo.findByIdForUpdate(cmd.toId())
            .orElseThrow(() -> new AccountNotFoundException(cmd.toId()));

        if (from.getBalance().compareTo(cmd.amount()) < 0) {
            throw new InsufficientFundsException();
        }

        from.debit(cmd.amount());
        to.credit(cmd.amount());
        transferRepo.save(new Transfer(from.getId(), to.getId(), cmd.amount()));

        accountRepo.save(from);
        accountRepo.save(to);
    }
}
// Portable, testable, observable — default architect choice

Error Mapping

java
try {
    paymentProcedureService.createPayment(cmd);
} catch (UncategorizedSQLException ex) {
    if (ex.getSQLException().getSQLState().equals("45000")) {
        throw new BusinessException("INVALID_PAYMENT");
    }
    throw ex;
}
// Better: define SQLSTATE or custom error codes in proc documentation

Flyway Migration

sql
-- db/migration/V30__sp_transfer_funds.sql
CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE sp_transfer_funds(...) ...;

-- Rollback strategy: V30_1__rollback_sp_transfer.sql with previous body

ORM and Stored Procedures

JPA @NamedStoredProcedureQuery

java
@Entity
@NamedStoredProcedureQuery(
    name = "Payment.create",
    procedureName = "sp_create_payment",
    parameters = {
        @StoredProcedureParameter(mode = ParameterMode.IN, name = "p_customer_id", type = Long.class),
        @StoredProcedureParameter(mode = ParameterMode.IN, name = "p_amount", type = BigDecimal.class),
        @StoredProcedureParameter(mode = ParameterMode.IN, name = "p_client_request_id", type = String.class),
        @StoredProcedureParameter(mode = ParameterMode.OUT, name = "p_payment_id", type = Long.class),

public class Payment { ... }

// Usage
StoredProcedureQuery q = em.createNamedStoredProcedureQuery("Payment.create");
q.setParameter("p_customer_id", 1001L);
// ...
q.execute();
Long paymentId = (Long) q.getOutputParameterValue("p_payment_id");

Limitations

text
❌ Hibernate does not map procedure results to entities automatically (unless REF CURSOR — Oracle)
❌ Mixing proc side effects + JPA persistence context — stale L1 cache
❌ @Transactional on service + proc internal COMMIT — broken session

✅ Use procedures outside JPA entity lifecycle — dedicated JDBC layer
✅ After CALL, em.clear() if mixing ORM reads in same session

When ORM + Proc Anti-Pattern

java
// ❌ Load entity, modify in Java, CALL proc that UPDATEs same row — conflict
Account a = accountRepo.findById(5001L);
sp.adjustBalance(5001L, 100);
accountRepo.save(a);  // overwrites proc changes with stale entity

// ✅ Either all proc OR all JPA in one transaction — not both on same rows

Part 15 — Architect Perspective

Stored Procedure Architecture

Decision Framework

text
                    ┌─────────────────────────┐
                    │ Need multi-step DB DML? │
                    └───────────┬─────────────┘
                                │
              ┌─────────────────┴─────────────────┐
              ▼                                   ▼
     Logic spans services?              Single service DB only?
     (payment + inventory)                      │
              │                                   │
              ▼                                   ▼
     Saga / outbox in Spring              @Transactional service
     NOT stored proc                              │
                                          Batch > 1M rows or
                                          legacy Oracle pkg?
                                                │
                                    ┌───────────┴───────────┐
                                    ▼                       ▼
                                   YES                      NO
                                    │                       │
                                    ▼                       ▼
                            Stored proc /              Java service
                            batch SQL job              + Flyway schema

Polyglot and Portability

text
PostgreSQL plpgsql ≠ Oracle PL/SQL ≠ T-SQL
Multi-DB product: avoid procs or abstract behind JDBC with dialect-specific Flyway folders
Single-DB enterprise (Oracle 20 years): procs are reality — wrap, don't rewrite blindly

Microservices Boundary

text
❌ Order Service CALLs Payment DB procedure — violates boundary
✅ Payment Service exposes REST/event; internal proc optional within Payment DB
✅ Shared nothing — no cross-DB CALL

Team Ownership

text
Schema + migrations: platform/DBA team
Procedure logic: who maintains PL/SQL in Java shop?
  → Often becomes orphan debt
  → If proc: assign explicit owner squad + integration tests

Observability Gap

text
Java: Micrometer, OpenTelemetry, structured logs
Proc: RAISE NOTICE, table audit log, pg_stat_user_functions

Architect requirement for proc-heavy systems:
  Audit table inside proc (who, when, params hash)
  External monitor on CALL duration via APM JDBC wrapper

Part 18 — Common Mistakes

Mistake 1: Business Logic Duplication

text
Java TransferService AND sp_transfer_funds both exist — rules diverge
Fix: one source of truth; proc OR Java, not both

Mistake 2: Row-by-Row Loop in Procedure

sql
-- ❌ 1M iterations
FOR r IN SELECT ... LOOP UPDATE ... END LOOP;
-- ✅ Set-based UPDATE

Mistake 3: COMMIT Inside Proc + Spring @Transactional

java
@Transactional
void job() {
    callProcWithInternalCommit();  // Spring txn state corrupted
}
// Batch jobs: call proc outside Spring txn or use propagation NOT_SUPPORTED

Mistake 4: No Version Control for Procedures

text
Manual hotfix in prod PL/SQL — Flyway drift
Fix: every change via migration + code review

Mistake 5: Swallowing Errors

sql
EXCEPTION WHEN OTHERS THEN NULL;  -- ❌ silent failure
-- ✅ RAISE or log to audit table + re-raise

Mistake 6: SECURITY DEFINER Without search_path Lock

sql
-- PostgreSQL attack: malicious search_path
CREATE PROCEDURE ... SECURITY DEFINER
SET search_path = pg_catalog, public AS $$ ... $$;
-- Always SET search_path on definer procs

Mistake 7: Using Procs for Cross-Service Workflow

sql
-- ❌ sp_place_order calls payment DB via dblink
-- ✅ Saga orchestrator in application layer

Part 19 — Interview Questions

Junior

Q1: What is a stored procedure?

Named procedural SQL stored in DB, invoked with CALL, accepts parameters, runs multiple statements.

Q2: IN vs OUT parameters?

IN: input from caller. OUT: returned to caller after execution.

Q3: Stored procedure vs function?

Procedure: side effects, CALL, no direct use in SELECT. Function: returns value, usable in expressions.

Q4: Can stored procedures improve performance?

Can reduce network round trips; does not fix bad SQL or missing indexes.

Q5: Where is procedure code stored?

Database catalog (pg_proc, ALL_SOURCE, sys.procedures) — not in application JAR unless mirrored in Flyway.

Mid-Level

Q6: Should transfer logic be in proc or Java?

Modern default: Java @Transactional with row locks. Proc: legacy, batch, or strict DB-side atomic requirement.

Q7: How call procedure from Spring?

SimpleJdbcCall, CallableStatement, or @NamedStoredProcedureQuery — prefer JDBC layer over mixing with JPA entities.

Q8: Transaction behavior when proc raises exception?

Entire transaction rolls back (unless savepoint). Spring marks rollback-only.

Q9: Flyway and procedures?

Version proc DDL in migrations; test in CI with Testcontainers.

Q10: Row-by-row vs set-based in procs?

Set-based SQL almost always faster; loops for exceptional control flow only.

Senior

Q11: AUTONOMOUS TRANSACTION use case?

Oracle: audit log that commits even if main txn rolls back — use sparingly; event outbox often better.

Q12: PostgreSQL PROCEDURE vs FUNCTION?

PG11+ PROCEDURE can COMMIT; FUNCTION cannot (traditionally) — use procedure for batch commit loops.

Q13: SECURITY DEFINER risks?

Runs as owner; privilege escalation if search_path or object names hijacked.

Q14: Strangler pattern for Oracle package?

Identify proc boundaries; extract read paths to Java; replace write paths incrementally; dual-run validation; deprecate package section by section.

Staff / Architect

Q15: Greenfield microservice — stored procs policy?

Default no business procs; schema migrations only; batch maintenance procs optional; document exceptions.

Q16: How observe proc-heavy legacy system?

JDBC timing, pg_stat_user_functions, audit tables, structured error codes, correlation ID passed as IN param.

Scenario

Scenario: "Team added sp_create_order with 800 lines PL/SQL; Java order service still exists."

Duplication debt. Architecture review: define single owner. Likely consolidate to Java + keep DB constraints; retain proc only if performance proof for batch path. Add integration test matrix comparing outcomes.

Lesson 22

Functions (User-Defined Functions)

Phase 2: SQL MASTERCLASS | Previous: Stored Procedures | Next: Triggers

SQL
1Concept2History3Problem Statement4Why This Exists5Internal Working6Storage Internals7Memory Usage8Execution Flow9Performance Analysis10Complexity Analysis11Code / SQL Examples12Production Usage13Spring Boot Integration14Hibernate/JPA Integration15Architect Perspective16Decision Matrix17Comparison Tables18Common Mistakes19Interview Questions20Revision Sheet21Summary Table*Practice

Part 1 — Concept

What Is a User-Defined Function (UDF)?

A user-defined function is a named routine stored in the database catalog that returns a value (scalar, row, or table) and is invoked inside SQL expressions — typically in SELECT, WHERE, JOIN, and CHECK constraints — unlike procedures which are invoked with CALL.

sql
-- PostgreSQL: scalar function
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION fn_account_available_balance(p_account_id BIGINT)
RETURNS NUMERIC(18,2)
LANGUAGE sql
STABLE
AS $$
    SELECT COALESCE(
        (SELECT balance FROM accounts
         WHERE account_id = p_account_id AND status = 'ACTIVE'),
        0
    );
$$;

-- Use in SELECT
SELECT account_id, balance, fn_account_available_balance(account_id) AS available
FROM accounts
WHERE status = 'ACTIVE';

Function vs Procedure vs View

text
┌─────────────┬──────────────────┬─────────────────────┬──────────────────┐
│             │ FUNCTION         │ PROCEDURE (L21)     │ VIEW (L20)       │
├─────────────┼──────────────────┼─────────────────────┼──────────────────┤
│ Invoke      │ fn(x) in SQL     │ CALL sp(x)          │ SELECT FROM v    │
│ Returns     │ Value / table    │ OUT params (side fx)│ Row set (query)  │
│ In SELECT   │ ✅ Yes           │ ❌ No               │ ✅ Yes           │
│ DML typical │ ❌ Avoid         │ ✅ Yes              │ ❌ Read-only     │
│ Side effects│ Discouraged      │ Expected            │ None             │
└─────────────┴──────────────────┴─────────────────────┴──────────────────┘

Function Classification

text
USER-DEFINED FUNCTIONS

├── By return shape
│   ├── Scalar function       → one value (INT, VARCHAR, NUMERIC)
│   ├── Table function        → set of rows (RETURNS TABLE)
│   └── Pipeline function     → RETURNS SETOF / TABLE (PostgreSQL)
│
├── By language
│   ├── SQL function          → body is SQL expression (inlinable)
│   ├── PL/pgSQL / PL/SQL     → procedural body with RETURN
│   └── External (C, Java)    → shared library / JVM in DB
│
├── By volatility (PostgreSQL)
│   ├── IMMUTABLE             → same inputs → same outputs, no DB reads
│   ├── STABLE                → same result within one statement scan
│   ├── VOLATILE              → default; may change (NOW(), random())
│   └── LEAKPROOF             → no side-channel info leak (security)
│
├── By purity
│   ├── Pure / deterministic  → safe for indexes, constraints
│   └── Impure                → time, random, session, DML inside
│
└── By SQL Server type
    ├── Inline TVF            → merged like view — fast
    └── Multi-statement TVF   → optimization fence — often slow

ASCII — Function in Query Plan

text
SELECT customer_id, fn_total_balance(customer_id) AS total
FROM customers
WHERE status = 'ACTIVE';

                    ┌─────────────────────┐
                    │   Seq/Index Scan    │
                    │   customers         │
                    └──────────┬──────────┘
                               │
                    ┌──────────▼──────────┐
                    │  Function Scan      │
                    │  fn_total_balance   │  ← per row OR inlined (SQL fn)
                    │  (customer_id)      │
                    └──────────┬──────────┘
                               │
                    ┌──────────▼──────────┐
                    │   Result rows       │
                    └─────────────────────┘

Part 2 — History

Evolution of Database Functions

text
1980s   Oracle PL/SQL functions in SELECT — financial calculations in DB
        Sybase/SQL Server user-defined functions for reusable expressions

1990s   SQL:1999 — scalar and table functions in standard
        Deterministic keyword (SQL Server) for index use on computed columns

2000s   PostgreSQL functions: SQL, plpgsql, multiple languages
        Criticism: scalar UDF per-row death in SQL Server pre-2019

2010s   PostgreSQL SQL functions inlined into caller query (major win)
        SQL Server 2019 scalar UDF inlining — finally addresses per-row cost
        Application layer preference: compute in Java for portability

2020s   PostgreSQL generated columns using IMMUTABLE functions
        Table functions + LATERAL for readable multi-row returns
        Cloud DBs: some restrict UDF languages for security

Historical Lesson

Scalar functions in SQL Server were notoriously slow (per-row invocation, no parallelism) until inline optimization arrived. PostgreSQL SQL functions can merge into the outer query like a macro. Architects must know: a function in SELECT is not free — volatility, inlining, and row-by-row execution matter enormously.

Part 3 — Problem Statement

What Problems Do Functions Solve?

Problem 1: Reusable Expression in Many Queries

sql
-- Mask PAN/card — same logic everywhere
CREATE FUNCTION fn_mask_account_no(p_acct VARCHAR) RETURNS VARCHAR AS $$
    SELECT '****' || RIGHT(p_acct, 4);
$$ LANGUAGE sql IMMUTABLE;

SELECT account_id, fn_mask_account_no(account_number) FROM accounts;
-- BI, reports, ad hoc SQL — one definition

Problem 2: Encapsulate Calculation (Domain Formula)

sql
CREATE FUNCTION fn_daily_interest(p_balance NUMERIC, p_rate NUMERIC)
RETURNS NUMERIC LANGUAGE sql IMMUTABLE AS $$
    SELECT ROUND(p_balance * p_rate / 365, 2);
$$;

SELECT account_id, fn_daily_interest(balance, annual_rate) AS interest
FROM accounts WHERE status = 'ACTIVE';

Problem 3: Table Function — Parameterized Row Source

sql
-- Accounts for customer as table-returning function — use with LATERAL
CREATE FUNCTION fn_customer_accounts(p_customer_id BIGINT)
RETURNS SETOF accounts AS $$
    SELECT * FROM accounts
    WHERE customer_id = p_customer_id AND status = 'ACTIVE';
$$ LANGUAGE sql STABLE;

SELECT c.customer_id, a.account_id, a.balance
FROM customers c
CROSS JOIN LATERAL fn_customer_accounts(c.customer_id) a;

Problem 4: Constraint / Generated Column (Pure Functions)

sql
-- Normalize email at write time
CREATE FUNCTION fn_normalize_email(p_email TEXT)
RETURNS TEXT LANGUAGE sql IMMUTABLE AS $$
    SELECT LOWER(TRIM(p_email));
$$;

ALTER TABLE customers
ADD COLUMN email_normalized TEXT
GENERATED ALWAYS AS (fn_normalize_email(email)) STORED;

Problem 5: Replace Repeated Subquery Pattern

sql
CREATE FUNCTION fn_customer_total_balance(p_customer_id BIGINT)
RETURNS NUMERIC LANGUAGE sql STABLE AS $$
    SELECT COALESCE(SUM(balance), 0)
    FROM accounts
    WHERE customer_id = p_customer_id AND status = 'ACTIVE';
$$;

SELECT customer_id, fn_customer_total_balance(customer_id) AS total
FROM customers WHERE region = 'APAC';
-- Optimizer may inline SQL function → same as subquery
-- Non-inlined plpgsql → per-row cost risk

Unified Problem Statement

Functions package reusable computations that return values for use inside SQL expressions — from simple scalar formulas to table-returning row sources — with volatility semantics that govern optimization and index eligibility.

Part 4 — Why This Exists

Why Functions vs Application Code vs Views?

vs View (Lesson 20)

text
View: fixed query, no parameters (except via WHERE by caller)
Function: parameterized logic — fn_balance(customer_id)

SELECT * FROM v_customer_balances WHERE customer_id = 1001;  -- view + filter
SELECT fn_customer_total_balance(1001);                        -- function call

vs Stored Procedure (Lesson 21)

text
Function: returns value, used in SELECT — read/compute focus
Procedure: CALL, side effects, OUT params — workflow focus

Need debit+credit transfer → procedure or @Transactional service
Need masked account number in report SELECT → function

vs Java Utility Method

DB FunctionJava Method
Use in SQLNativeMust pull rows to app
BI toolsDirectCannot
PortabilityDB-specificPortable
Unit testDB integrationJUnit
Index on expressionIMMUTABLE fn in PGN/A in DB

When Functions Fit Architecturally

text
✅ Pure formatting, normalization (IMMUTABLE)
✅ Shared expression in SQL reports / constraints
✅ Table function + LATERAL for parameterized joins
✅ Legacy Oracle fn_* used across 200 reports

❌ Business workflow with DML → procedure or service
❌ Heavy aggregation on billion rows in scalar fn per row
❌ Logic that changes weekly — Java deploy faster than Flyway fn churn

Part 5 — Internal Working

How Functions Execute Internally

PostgreSQL SQL Function — Inlining

sql
CREATE FUNCTION fn_active_balance(p_cid BIGINT) RETURNS NUMERIC
LANGUAGE sql STABLE AS $$
    SELECT COALESCE(SUM(balance),0) FROM accounts
    WHERE customer_id = p_cid AND status = 'ACTIVE';
$$;

SELECT customer_id, fn_active_balance(customer_id) FROM customers;
text
OPTIMIZER (function inlining):

  Expand to:
  SELECT customer_id,
         (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(balance),0) FROM accounts
          WHERE customer_id = customers.customer_id AND status = 'ACTIVE')
  FROM customers;

  May further optimize to JOIN + GROUP BY or subquery initplan
  STABLE: can cache result within statement for same p_cid
  IMMUTABLE: stronger optimizations (index expressions)

PostgreSQL PL/pgSQL Function — Non-Inlined

sql
CREATE FUNCTION fn_active_balance_plpgsql(p_cid BIGINT) RETURNS NUMERIC
LANGUAGE plpgsql STABLE AS $$
DECLARE v NUMERIC;
BEGIN
    SELECT COALESCE(SUM(balance),0) INTO v FROM accounts
    WHERE customer_id = p_cid AND status = 'ACTIVE';
    RETURN v;
END;
$$;
text
Plan often shows:
  Function Scan on fn_active_balance_plpgsql
  → Per-row invocation overhead (context switch PL/pgSQL ↔ SQL)

Prefer LANGUAGE sql when body is single SELECT expression
Use plpgsql when control flow needed — accept cost

Volatility Semantics (PostgreSQL)

text
IMMUTABLE:
  Cannot read DB, no NOW(), no side effects
  Same args → same result forever
  → Index expressions, generated columns, optimizer constant folding

STABLE:
  Same args → same result within ONE SQL statement
  Can read DB (snapshot consistent in statement)
  → Most read-only lookups from tables

VOLATILE (default):
  NOW(), random(), writes, session settings
  → Re-evaluated as needed; no aggressive caching

SQL Server Scalar UDF

text
Pre-2019: often per-row, serial, slow
2019+ with inline: IF scalar UDF meets inline criteria → merged
Multi-statement TVF: table variable → optimization fence (slow)
Inline TVF: merged like view — preferred pattern

Oracle Function

text
SQL function / PL/SQL function
DETERMINISTIC keyword (similar to IMMUTABLE hint)
Function-based indexes: CREATE INDEX ON t(fn_col(x))
PIPELINED table functions for row-by-row emit (advanced)

Table Function + LATERAL

sql
SELECT * FROM customers c,
LATERAL fn_customer_accounts(c.customer_id) a;

Planner:
  Nested loop: for each customer → execute table function
  Or merge SQL table function if inlinable
  Index on accounts(customer_id) critical

Part 6 — Storage Internals

Functions and Storage

Catalog Storage Only (Definition)

text
Function metadata in pg_proc / ALL_OBJECTS / sys.objects
Source or compiled bytecode — kilobytes
No data files for function itself

Function Reads/Writes Base Tables

text
STABLE function querying accounts:
  Same I/O as subquery — reads heap/index pages
  No caching across statements (unless app or mat view caches)

VOLATILE function with INSERT inside (anti-pattern):
  Writes WAL like normal DML — hidden side effect in SELECT

Generated Column / Index on Function

sql
CREATE INDEX idx_customers_email_norm ON customers (fn_normalize_email(email));

-- Index stores computed normalized values — extra disk
-- INSERT/UPDATE maintains index entry when email changes
-- Requires IMMUTABLE function

SQL Server Inline TVF

text
No intermediate table storage — merged plan
Multi-statement TVF uses table variable — tempdb spill possible

Part 7 — Memory Usage

Function Memory Impact

PatternMemory
Inlined SQL scalar fnMerged plan — no extra per call
PL/pgSQL per-row fnFunction call frame — CPU + small stack per row
Table function (set returning)Tuplestore for result set per invocation
LATERAL fn per outer rown × function execution — can be heavy
Oracle pipelined fnIncremental — lower peak memory
Aggregate in fn called per rowRepeated subquery work — worse than JOIN

Danger: Scalar Function on Large Scan

sql
-- 10M rows — fn called 10M times if not inlined
SELECT account_id, fn_complex_calc(balance) FROM accounts;

-- EXPLAIN ANALYZE — watch Function Scan loops=10000000
-- Fix: inline SQL, JOIN precomputed, or batch in app

Part 8 — Execution Flow

Function Execution Flows

Flow 1: IMMUTABLE Scalar in SELECT List

sql
SELECT customer_id, fn_mask_account_no(account_number) FROM accounts LIMIT 100;
text
1. Scan accounts (100 rows if limit pushed — depends on plan)
2. For each row: evaluate fn_mask_account_no — pure CPU, no I/O
3. IMMUTABLE: may compute at parse time if arg constant
4. Return result set

Flow 2: STABLE Function with DB Lookup

sql
SELECT c.customer_id, fn_customer_total_balance(c.customer_id)
FROM customers c WHERE c.region = 'APAC';
text
1. Scan/filter customers APAC — 50K rows
2. If inlined: transform to LEFT JOIN accounts + GROUP BY or correlated subquery
3. If not inlined: 50K function invocations — each SUM query
4. STABLE cache: same customer_id twice in one statement → second may use cache (PG)

Flow 3: Function in WHERE (Sargability Risk)

sql
SELECT * FROM customers
WHERE fn_normalize_email(email) = 'user@bank.com';
text
❌ Non-sargable: cannot use index on email directly
✅ Fix: compare normalized column:
WHERE email_normalized = fn_normalize_email('user@bank.com')
   OR use generated column + index on email_normalized

Flow 4: Table Function in FROM

sql
SELECT c.email, a.account_id, a.balance
FROM customers c
CROSS JOIN LATERAL fn_customer_accounts(c.customer_id) a
WHERE c.customer_id = 1001;
text
1. Filter customer 1001 — one row
2. Execute table function once → index scan accounts by customer_id
3. Return joined rows
Efficient for selective outer query

Flow 5: Function in CHECK Constraint

sql
ALTER TABLE payments ADD CONSTRAINT chk_amount_positive
CHECK (fn_is_valid_amount(amount));

-- Every INSERT/UPDATE evaluates function
-- Must be IMMUTABLE or STABLE — not VOLATILE with NOW()
-- Failure → constraint violation before commit

Part 9 — Performance Analysis

Function Performance Rules

Performance Hierarchy

text
FAST:
  LANGUAGE sql + STABLE/IMMUTABLE — inlined by PostgreSQL
  IMMUTABLE pure CPU (mask, format)
  Inline TVF (SQL Server)
  Table function with selective LATERAL outer filter + index

SLOW:
  PL/pgSQL scalar fn on millions of rows (not inlined)
  Multi-statement TVF (SQL Server)
  VOLATILE fn preventing optimization
  Function in WHERE on column — full table scan
  Scalar fn wrapping aggregate — per-row subquery

ALWAYS: EXPLAIN ANALYZE with and without function

Function in SELECT vs JOIN Precompute

sql
-- ❌ Per-row function doing SUM
SELECT c.*, fn_customer_total_balance(c.customer_id) FROM customers c;

-- ✅ Often faster
SELECT c.*, t.total
FROM customers c
LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT customer_id, SUM(balance) AS total
    FROM accounts WHERE status = 'ACTIVE' GROUP BY customer_id
) t ON t.customer_id = c.customer_id;

When Function in Index Helps

sql
-- Queries always filter by normalized email
CREATE INDEX idx_cust_email_norm ON customers (fn_normalize_email(email));
-- WHERE fn_normalize_email(email) = ?  → index scan
-- Function must be IMMUTABLE and marked correctly

SQL Server Specific

text
Prefer inline TVF over multi-statement TVF
Enable scalar UDF inlining (2019+) — verify with execution plan
Avoid scalar UDF in hot OLTP UPDATE triggers

Part 10 — Complexity Analysis

PatternTimeNotes
IMMUTABLE scalar per rowO(n) CPUn = rows
STABLE fn with DB read, not inlinedO(n × lookup)Can be O(n × m) disaster
Inlined SQL functionO(merged plan)Often O(n) or O(n log n)
Table fn + LATERAL, outer n rowsO(n × f)f = inner cost; index → O(n log m)
Generated column index lookupO(log n)Per query

Part 11 — Code / SQL Examples

Function Masterclass

IMMUTABLE — Formatting and Validation

sql
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION fn_mask_email(p_email TEXT)
RETURNS TEXT
LANGUAGE sql
IMMUTABLE
AS $$
    SELECT CASE
        WHEN p_email IS NULL OR position('@' IN p_email) = 0 THEN '***'
        ELSE LEFT(p_email, 2) || '***@' || split_part(p_email, '@', 2)
    END;
$$;

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION fn_is_valid_currency(p_code CHAR(3))
RETURNS BOOLEAN
LANGUAGE sql
IMMUTABLE
AS $$
    SELECT p_code IN ('USD', 'EUR', 'GBP', 'INR', 'SGD');
$$;

STABLE — Balance Lookup

sql
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION fn_customer_total_balance(p_customer_id BIGINT)
RETURNS NUMERIC(18,2)
LANGUAGE sql
STABLE
AS $$
    SELECT COALESCE(SUM(balance), 0)
    FROM accounts
    WHERE customer_id = p_customer_id
      AND status = 'ACTIVE';
$$;

SELECT customer_id, email, fn_customer_total_balance(customer_id) AS total
FROM customers
WHERE status = 'ACTIVE'
  AND fn_customer_total_balance(customer_id) > 100000;
-- Better: filter via JOIN to avoid double evaluation

Table Function — RETURNS TABLE

sql
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION fn_payments_in_range(
    p_customer_id BIGINT,
    p_from TIMESTAMPTZ,
    p_to TIMESTAMPTZ
)
RETURNS TABLE (
    payment_id BIGINT,
    amount NUMERIC(18,2),
    status VARCHAR(20),
    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ
)
LANGUAGE sql
STABLE
AS $$
    SELECT payment_id, amount, status, created_at
    FROM payments
    WHERE customer_id = p_customer_id
      AND created_at BETWEEN p_from AND p_to
      AND status = 'COMPLETED';
$$;

SELECT c.customer_id, p.*
FROM customers c
CROSS JOIN LATERAL fn_payments_in_range(
    c.customer_id,
    CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '30 days',
    NOW()
) p
WHERE c.customer_id = 1001;

PL/pgSQL — Control Flow (Use Sparingly)

sql
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION fn_account_status_label(p_account_id BIGINT)
RETURNS TEXT
LANGUAGE plpgsql
STABLE
AS $$
DECLARE
    v_status TEXT;
    v_balance NUMERIC;
BEGIN
    SELECT status, balance INTO v_status, v_balance
    FROM accounts WHERE account_id = p_account_id;

    IF NOT FOUND THEN
        RETURN 'UNKNOWN';
    ELSIF v_status = 'SUSPENDED' THEN
        RETURN 'SUSPENDED';
    ELSIF v_balance < 0 THEN
        RETURN 'OVERDRAWN';
    ELSE
        RETURN 'OK';
    END IF;
END;
$$;

Oracle — Deterministic Function + Index

sql
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION fn_upper_email(p_email VARCHAR2)
RETURN VARCHAR2 DETERMINISTIC IS
BEGIN
    RETURN UPPER(TRIM(p_email));
END;
/

CREATE INDEX idx_cust_upper_email ON customers (fn_upper_email(email));

SQL Server — Inline Table-Valued Function

sql
CREATE FUNCTION dbo.fn_active_accounts(@customer_id BIGINT)
RETURNS TABLE
AS
RETURN (
    SELECT account_id, balance, account_type
    FROM dbo.accounts
    WHERE customer_id = @customer_id AND status = 'ACTIVE'
);

SELECT c.customer_id, a.*
FROM dbo.customers c
CROSS APPLY dbo.fn_active_accounts(c.customer_id) a;

Generated Column (PostgreSQL)

sql
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION fn_normalize_email(p TEXT)
RETURNS TEXT LANGUAGE sql IMMUTABLE AS $$
    SELECT LOWER(TRIM(p));
$$;

ALTER TABLE customers
ADD COLUMN email_normalized TEXT
GENERATED ALWAYS AS (fn_normalize_email(email)) STORED;

CREATE INDEX idx_customers_email_norm ON customers (email_normalized);

Anti-Pattern — Side Effects in Function

sql
-- ❌ NEVER: DML in function used in SELECT
CREATE FUNCTION fn_log_and_return(x INT) RETURNS INT AS $$
BEGIN
    INSERT INTO audit_log VALUES (x);  -- hidden write
    RETURN x;
END;
$$ LANGUAGE plpgsql VOLATILE;
-- Violates expectations; use trigger or explicit proc

Part 12 — Production Usage

Functions in Production

Banking — Masking in Reports

sql
-- Shared masking for all SQL consumers (BI, Grafana SQL, support tools)
CREATE FUNCTION fn_mask_pan(p VARCHAR) RETURNS VARCHAR
LANGUAGE sql IMMUTABLE AS $$
    SELECT CASE WHEN length(p) < 4 THEN '****'
                ELSE repeat('*', length(p)-4) || right(p,4) END;
$$;

-- Grant EXECUTE to reporting_role
-- Do NOT rely on app-only masking if DB tools access raw tables

Payments — Currency Validation

sql
CHECK (fn_is_valid_currency(currency))
-- Constraint enforced at DB regardless of app bug

E-Commerce — Pricing Function (Careful)

sql
-- Simple tier discount — if rules stable
CREATE FUNCTION fn_loyalty_discount(p_tier INT, p_amount NUMERIC)
RETURNS NUMERIC LANGUAGE sql IMMUTABLE AS $$
    SELECT CASE p_tier
        WHEN 3 THEN p_amount * 0.90
        WHEN 2 THEN p_amount * 0.95
        ELSE p_amount
    END;
$$;
-- If pricing changes daily → Java/pricing service, not IMMUTABLE lie

When NOT to Use UDF in Production OLTP

text
❌ fn_get_balance(account_id) on every row of batch UPDATE
❌ Complex pricing rules that change with A/B tests — deploy in app
❌ Function calling external network (some DBs allow — forbidden pattern)
❌ Marking VOLATILE function IMMUTABLE — wrong results + corrupt indexes
✅ Pure format/normalize with correct volatility
✅ SQL STABLE functions inlined for reports on replica
✅ Table functions for parameterized report slices

sql
-- db/migration/V40__fn_customer_total_balance.sql
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION fn_customer_total_balance(...) ...;

-- DROP INDEX IF EXISTS idx_...; CREATE OR REPLACE ...; CREATE INDEX ...

Avoid Calling UDF Per Entity in Loop

Part 14 — Hibernate/JPA Integration

ORM and Functions

JPQL — Limited Built-in Functions

java
// JPQL has CONCAT, LENGTH, SUBSTRING — not custom UDF
@Query("SELECT c FROM Customer c WHERE LOWER(c.email) = LOWER(:email)")
// Portable — no fn_normalize_email in JPQL standard

Hibernate @Formula (Scalar Function Mapping)

java
@Entity
public class Customer {

    @Id
    private Long customerId;

    @Formula("fn_customer_total_balance(customer_id)")
    private BigDecimal totalBalance;  // computed on read — N+1 risk if lazy pattern wrong
}
// ⚠️ Read-only; DB-specific; breaks portability
// ⚠️ Every load triggers function — prefer explicit query or JOIN DTO

Database Function Registration (Hibernate 6+)

java
// Some dialects allow registerFunction for HQL — rarely used for custom business fn
// Native query remains practical approach

Best Practice

text
❌ @Formula fn_* on hot @Entity — hidden per-row cost
✅ Explicit native query or view (Lesson 20) for computed columns
✅ DTO projection with JOIN + SUM in JPQL (portable)
✅ IMMUTABLE normalization → generated column + map plain field

Part 15 — Architect Perspective

Function Architecture Decisions

Function vs View vs Service Utility

text
Parameterized row source for reports     → Table function or view + WHERE
Fixed join shape reused everywhere       → View
Pure format/mask in SQL tools             → IMMUTABLE function
Complex business rules, frequent change  → Java domain service
Constraint enforcement (simple)          → IMMUTABLE CHECK function
Multi-step write workflow                → Procedure or @Transactional service

Volatility Honesty Policy

text
Architecture standard:

IMMUTABLE  → no table reads, no clock, no random — code review required
STABLE     → read-only snapshot queries OK
VOLATILE   → default; document why; never in indexes/generated columns

Wrong label → silent wrong answers + index corruption

Multi-Database Strategy

text
PostgreSQL plpgsql + SQL Server T-SQL + Oracle PL/SQL — not portable
Shared logic in Java for product core
DB functions only for:
  - SQL reporting layer per deployment
  - Performance-proven expressions with Flyway per dialect folder
    db/migration/postgresql/V40__fn.sql
    db/migration/oracle/V40__fn.sql

Microservices

text
Functions live inside service database — not shared across services
Payment fn_calculate_fee used only in Payment DB reports
Order service does not CALL Payment DB functions

Part 18 — Common Mistakes

Mistake 1: Wrong Volatility Label

sql
-- ❌ Reads accounts but marked IMMUTABLE
CREATE FUNCTION fn_balance(p BIGINT) RETURNS NUMERIC IMMUTABLE AS $$
    SELECT balance FROM accounts WHERE account_id = p;
$$ LANGUAGE sql;
-- Corrupt indexes, wrong optimization

-- ✅ STABLE

Mistake 2: Function in WHERE on Column

sql
WHERE fn_normalize_email(email) = :email  -- seq scan
-- ✅ WHERE email_normalized = :normalized  -- index

Mistake 3: PL/pgSQL Scalar on Millions of Rows

SELECT fn_heavy_plpgsql(account_id) FROM accounts;  -- Function Scan hell
-- ✅ LANGUAGE sql for inlining or rewrite as JOIN

Mistake 4: Hidden DML in Function

sql
-- Audit insert inside fn used in SELECT — surprises, locks, WAL
-- Use trigger or explicit audit in service

Mistake 5: @Formula on Entity

java
@Formula("fn_customer_total_balance(customer_id)")
// Loads 500 customers → 500 function calls
// ✅ Batch query with JOIN

Mistake 6: SQL Server Multi-Statement TVF

sql
-- Slow optimization fence — rewrite as inline TVF
RETURNS @table TABLE (...) BEGIN INSERT @table ... RETURN END

Mistake 7: Changing Function Signature Without Cascade

sql
-- DROP FUNCTION fails — index depends on it
-- Migration: DROP INDEX → REPLACE FUNCTION → CREATE INDEX

Part 19 — Interview Questions

Junior

Q1: Function vs stored procedure?

Function returns value for use in SQL expressions; procedure invoked with CALL for workflows/side effects.

Q2: Can you use a function in WHERE clause?

Yes, but wrapping columns (fn(col) = x) often prevents index use — prefer sargable form.

Q3: What does IMMUTABLE mean in PostgreSQL?

Same arguments always same result; no DB reads; safe for indexes and generated columns.

Q4: Scalar vs table function?

Scalar returns one value; table function returns set of rows.

Q5: Where is function code stored?

Database catalog — versioned via Flyway like tables and views.

Mid-Level

Q6: STABLE vs VOLATILE?

STABLE: consistent within one statement scan. VOLATILE: can change anytime (NOW(), writes).

Q7: Why were SQL Server scalar UDFs historically slow?

Per-row invocation without inlining; blocked parallelism pre-2019.

Q8: PostgreSQL LANGUAGE sql vs plpgsql performance?

SQL functions often inlined into query; plpgsql usually Function Scan per row.

Q9: LATERAL with table function — purpose?

Correlated row source — function parameters from outer row.

Q10: Function in CHECK constraint requirements?

Must be deterministic/stable; no side effects; failure aborts DML.

Senior

Q11: When mark function IMMUTABLE incorrectly breaks system?

Wrong index results, invalid generated columns, optimizer constant folding errors.

Q12: Rewrite fn_customer_total_balance per-row to set-based SQL.

JOIN (SELECT customer_id, SUM(balance) ...) t ON c.customer_id = t.customer_id

Q13: Inline TVF vs multi-statement TVF SQL Server?

Inline merges like view; multi-statement uses table variable — avoid for perf.

Q14: Hibernate @Formula tradeoffs?

Hidden DB coupling, per-load cost, not portable — use DTO query instead.

Staff / Architect

Q15: Policy: custom functions in microservice DB?

Allow IMMUTABLE format/normalize; STABLE report helpers on replica; business rules in Java unless proven SQL-only consumer need.

Q16: Multi-dialect product with Oracle + PostgreSQL functions?

Dialect-specific Flyway folders or minimize UDFs — shared logic in application.

Scenario

Scenario: "Report SELECT with fn_balance(account_id) on 20M accounts takes hours."

EXPLAIN — Function Scan 20M loops. Replace with JOIN to accounts or inline SQL function; ensure not plpgsql; run on replica; pre-aggregate mat view if recurring.

1Concept2History3Problem Statement4Why This Exists5Internal Working6Storage Internals7Memory Usage8Execution Flow9Performance Analysis10Complexity Analysis11Code / SQL Examples12Production Usage13Spring Boot Integration14Hibernate/JPA Integration15Architect Perspective16Decision Matrix17Comparison Tables18Common Mistakes19Interview Questions20Revision Sheet21Summary Table*Practice

Part 1 — Concept

What Is a Trigger?

A trigger is a stored program automatically executed by the database when a specific event occurs — typically INSERT, UPDATE, or DELETE on a table (or database-level events in some systems). Triggers run without explicit CALL from application code.

sql
-- PostgreSQL: audit trigger on payments
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION trg_fn_audit_payment()
RETURNS TRIGGER
LANGUAGE plpgsql
AS $$
BEGIN
    INSERT INTO payments_audit (
        payment_id, operation, old_amount, new_amount,
        changed_at, changed_by
    ) VALUES (
        COALESCE(NEW.payment_id, OLD.payment_id),
        TG_OP,
        OLD.amount,
        NEW.amount,
        NOW(),
        current_user
    );
    RETURN COALESCE(NEW, OLD);
END;
$$;

CREATE TRIGGER trg_payments_audit
AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE OR DELETE ON payments
FOR EACH ROW
EXECUTE FUNCTION trg_fn_audit_payment();

Trigger vs Procedure vs Constraint

text
┌──────────────┬─────────────────┬──────────────────┬─────────────────────┐
│              │ TRIGGER         │ PROCEDURE (L21)  │ CONSTRAINT (L7)     │
├──────────────┼─────────────────┼──────────────────┼─────────────────────┤
│ Invocation   │ Automatic       │ CALL / EXEC      │ Automatic on DML      │
│ Purpose      │ Audit, side fx  │ Workflow         │ Data integrity      │
│ Visibility   │ Hidden from app │ Explicit         │ Declarative           │
│ Return       │ BEFORE: NEW/OLD │ OUT params       │ Pass/fail             │
│ Business     │ Often anti-     │ Batch/workflow   │ Simple rules          │
│ logic        │ pattern         │                  │                       │
└──────────────┴─────────────────┴──────────────────┴─────────────────────┘

Trigger Classification

text
TRIGGERS

├── By timing
│   ├── BEFORE          → runs before row/event applied; can modify NEW
│   ├── AFTER           → runs after change; audit, replication fan-out
│   └── INSTEAD OF      → on views (Lesson 20); replaces DML
│
├── By granularity
│   ├── FOR EACH ROW    → once per affected row (most common)
│   └── FOR EACH STATEMENT → once per SQL statement (bulk ops)
│
├── By event
│   ├── INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE
│   ├── TRUNCATE (statement-level)
│   └── DDL triggers (Oracle, SQL Server — specialized)
│
├── By scope
│   ├── Table trigger
│   └── Database trigger (Oracle SYS, SQL Server DDL)
│
└── By role
    ├── Audit trigger       → append-only log
    ├── Enforcement trigger → validate (prefer CHECK/FK)
    ├── Derivation trigger  → maintain derived columns/tables
    └── Integration trigger → queue/outbox (legacy pattern)

ASCII — Trigger Firing Order

text
Application: INSERT INTO payments (...)

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ 1. BEFORE STATEMENT triggers (if any)                       │
│ 2. For each row:                                            │
│      a. BEFORE ROW triggers  → may modify NEW, or RAISE     │
│      b. Apply row to table (constraints checked)            │
│      c. AFTER ROW triggers   → audit, side effects          │
│ 3. AFTER STATEMENT triggers (if any)                        │
│ 4. COMMIT (if in transaction)                               │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Part 2 — History

Evolution of Triggers

text
1980s   Oracle row triggers — audit and derived column maintenance
        Sybase triggers for referential integrity before declarative FK widespread

1990s   SQL:1999 standardizes trigger concept
        BEFORE/AFTER, row/statement granularity
        "Trigger hell" in enterprise schemas — opaque cascading logic

2000s   Declarative constraints preferred: FK, CHECK, UNIQUE
        Hibernate/JPA — triggers invisible to ORM; surprise side effects
        Replication tools (GoldenGate, Debezium) replace trigger-based CDC

2010s   Event-driven architecture — outbox pattern in app vs trigger queues
        PostgreSQL: powerful row triggers + NOTIFY; transition tables (PG10+)
        Audit requirements (SOX, PCI) keep AFTER triggers common

2020s   Default architect stance: **minimal triggers** — audit + updated_at
        Change Data Capture (CDC) from WAL preferred over custom audit triggers
        PostgreSQL RLS + policies vs trigger-based row security (legacy)

Historical Lesson

Triggers were the only way to enforce cross-row rules before mature constraints and application frameworks. Today they remain valuable for audit trails and database-enforced invariants that must never be bypassed — but cascading trigger logic becomes undebuggable distributed monolith inside the DB. Architects cap trigger use with explicit governance.

Part 3 — Problem Statement

What Problems Do Triggers Solve?

Problem 1: Audit Trail (Who Changed What, When)

sql
-- Every payment amount change logged — even from DBA SQL client
AFTER UPDATE ON payments → INSERT INTO payments_audit
-- Application cannot "forget" to audit if trigger exists

Problem 2: Automatic Timestamp Maintenance

sql
BEFORE UPDATE ON accounts
FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION trg_set_updated_at();
-- NEW.updated_at := NOW(); — consistent across all writers

Problem 3: Derived Data Synchronization

sql
-- Maintain customer_balance_summary when accounts.balance changes
AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE OR DELETE ON accounts
FOR EACH ROW → UPDATE customer_balance_summary SET total = ...
-- Alternative: materialized view refresh, app event, or compute on read

Problem 4: Enforce Rule Not Expressible as CHECK

sql
-- Cannot CHECK across tables easily — trigger validates
BEFORE INSERT ON transfers
FOR EACH ROW → IF NOT fn_account_active(NEW.from_account_id) THEN RAISE ...
-- Often better: FK + status check + service layer

Problem 5: INSTEAD OF View DML (Lesson 20)

sql
INSTEAD OF INSERT ON v_account_customer
FOR EACH ROW → INSERT INTO accounts ...; INSERT INTO customers ...;

Unified Problem Statement

Triggers react automatically to data changes — guaranteeing side effects (audit, timestamps, derived updates) that no application path can skip, at the cost of hidden logic and performance overhead.

Part 4 — Why This Exists

Why Triggers vs Application Logic?

Guarantees Across All Writers

text
Writers to payments table:
  - Spring Boot API
  - Batch SQL script
  - DBA manual fix
  - ETL job
  - pgAdmin

Application audit service only covers API path ❌
AFTER trigger covers ALL paths ✅

Colocation with Data

text
Audit row inserted in same transaction as payment UPDATE
Atomic: payment change + audit both commit or both rollback
App-level audit after commit → gap if app crashes

Why Teams Avoid Heavy Trigger Logic

text
❌ Hidden from code review (Flyway only)
❌ ORM batch insert → trigger fires N times — surprise slowness
❌ Cascading triggers — table A → trigger → update B → trigger on B
❌ Hard to unit test without DB
❌ Duplicate rule in Java + trigger
❌ Debugging "who changed this row?" — need trigger source archaeology

Modern Alternatives

NeedTriggerModern Alternative
AuditAFTER triggerCDC (Debezium), temporal tables
updated_atBEFORE trigger@UpdateTimestamp, JPA @PreUpdate
Cross-table ruleBEFORE triggerService @Transactional + FK
Outbox/eventsAFTER trigger INSERT queueTransactional outbox in app
Derived aggregateAFTER triggerAsync consumer, mat view

Architect Default

text
Allowed without debate: audit (AFTER), updated_at (BEFORE)
Requires ADR approval: cross-table updates, business rules in triggers
Forbidden: HTTP calls, file I/O, long-running work in triggers

Part 5 — Internal Working

How Triggers Execute Internally

Trigger Function vs Trigger Definition (PostgreSQL)

text
CREATE FUNCTION trg_fn_...() RETURNS TRIGGER  -- logic
CREATE TRIGGER trg_name ... EXECUTE FUNCTION trg_fn_...();  -- binding

Oracle: CREATE TRIGGER ... BEGIN ... END;  -- inline or calls procedure
SQL Server: CREATE TRIGGER ... AS BEGIN ... END

BEFORE ROW — Modify or Reject

sql
BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE ON payments FOR EACH ROW
text
For each row:
  1. Engine constructs NEW (and OLD for UPDATE/DELETE) row image in memory
  2. Runs trigger function with transition variables NEW, OLD
  3. Trigger may:
     - RETURN NEW → proceed with possibly modified NEW
     - RETURN NULL → skip row (INSERT/UPDATE cancel for that row — PG)
     - RAISE EXCEPTION → abort entire statement
  4. Constraints (CHECK, FK) evaluated on final NEW
  5. Row written to heap + indexes

AFTER ROW — Side Effects

text
Row already written to table (visible in same txn)
Trigger runs:
  - INSERT audit row
  - UPDATE summary table
  - NOTIFY channel (PG)
Cannot modify original row (RETURN ignored)
Errors abort transaction — payment + audit both rollback

Statement-Level Triggers

sql
AFTER INSERT ON payments
REFERENCING NEW TABLE AS inserted
FOR EACH STATEMENT
EXECUTE FUNCTION trg_fn_validate_batch();
text
Fires once per INSERT statement regardless of row count
PostgreSQL 10+ transition tables: NEW TABLE / OLD TABLE see all rows
Useful: batch validation, aggregate check after bulk load
Rare compared to row triggers

Firing Order (Multiple Triggers)

text
PostgreSQL: alphabetical trigger name by default (configurable)
Oracle: FOLLOWS / PRECEDES (12c+)
Unpredictable order → dangerous if triggers depend on each other
Best: one trigger per table per event, or explicit ordering

Constraint vs Trigger Timing

text
Typical order (PostgreSQL simplified):
  BEFORE ROW triggers
  Check constraints / NOT NULL
  Row write
  AFTER ROW triggers
  AFTER STATEMENT triggers
  FK checks may be DEFERRABLE — end of txn

Part 6 — Storage Internals

Triggers and Storage

Trigger Definition — Catalog Only

text
pg_trigger, ALL_TRIGGERS, sys.triggers — metadata kilobytes

Audit Trigger — Extra Writes

text
One payment UPDATE → one audit INSERT
WAL records for BOTH:
  UPDATE payments heap + indexes
  INSERT payments_audit heap + indexes

2× write amplification minimum for audited tables
High-churn OLTP: audit table growth — partition, archive, TTL

Derived Table Maintenance Trigger

text
UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance + 100 WHERE account_id = 5001

AFTER trigger UPDATE customer_balance_summary:
  Additional row lock on summary row
  Potential hot row contention — one summary row per customer, many accounts updating

Index Impact

text
Audit table indexes on (payment_id, changed_at):
  Every audit INSERT maintains indexes
  Consider heap-only audit with async ETL to warehouse for analytics

Hibernate Batch Insert

java
// 500 inserts in JDBC batch
INSERT INTO payments ... (batch 500)
→ 500 BEFORE row triggers + 500 AFTER row triggers + 500 audit INSERTs
→ Effectively 1500+ operations — batch benefit reduced

Part 7 — Memory Usage

Trigger Memory Impact

AspectImpact
NEW/OLD row imagesPer-row memory in trigger context
plpgsql variablesSmall stack per invocation
Statement trigger + transition tableMaterialize all new rows in memory/temp
Cascading triggersMultiplicative work — not always multiplicative memory
NOTIFY in triggerQueue message — small

Transition Tables (PostgreSQL)

sql
REFERENCING NEW TABLE AS new_rows
-- Bulk INSERT 100K rows → NEW TABLE holds 100K rows for statement trigger
-- work_mem / temp storage for large bulk loads

Recursive Trigger Risk

sql
-- Trigger on A updates B; trigger on B updates A
-- Infinite loop until max depth or lock error
-- Need guard: IF pg_trigger_depth() > 1 THEN RETURN NEW;

Part 8 — Execution Flow

Trigger Execution Flows

Flow 1: AFTER Audit on UPDATE

text
1. BEGIN (Spring @Transactional)
2. UPDATE payments SET amount=300 WHERE payment_id=9001
3. BEFORE triggers (none)
4. Row updated in payments
5. AFTER trigger: INSERT payments_audit (OLD.amount=250, NEW.amount=300)
6. COMMIT — both visible
7. Hibernate session may have stale Payment entity if amount changed again in trigger (rare)

Flow 2: BEFORE — Reject Invalid Transfer

text
1. INSERT INTO transfers (from_id, to_id, amount) VALUES (5001, 5002, -100)
2. BEFORE INSERT trigger: IF NEW.amount <= 0 RAISE EXCEPTION
3. Statement aborted — no row inserted
4. Spring: DataIntegrityViolationException / UncategorizedSQLException

Flow 3: BEFORE — Set updated_at

text
1. UPDATE accounts SET balance = 9000 WHERE account_id = 5001
2. BEFORE UPDATE: NEW.updated_at := NOW()
3. Row written with new balance and timestamp
4. App didn't set updatedAt — DB guarantees consistency

Flow 4: Cascading Summary Maintenance

text
1. UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance + 500 WHERE customer_id = 1001  -- 3 rows
2. AFTER ROW trigger fires 3 times
3. Each: UPDATE customer_balance_summary SET total = total + delta
   OR worse: recalc SUM from all accounts each time — 3 full aggregates
4. Lock contention on summary row for customer 1001

Flow 5: INSTEAD OF on View

text
1. UPDATE v_account_email SET email = 'new@bank.com' WHERE account_id = 5001
2. INSTEAD OF UPDATE trigger runs
3. Trigger UPDATEs customers SET email = ... WHERE customer_id = ...
4. Base tables updated — view is not physical

Part 9 — Performance Analysis

Trigger Performance Rules

Performance Hierarchy

text
CHEAP:
  BEFORE updated_at assignment — O(1) per row
  AFTER audit INSERT with narrow row — O(1) per row, sequential insert

EXPENSIVE:
  AFTER trigger recalculates SUM from child table per row — O(n) per fire
  Cascading triggers across many tables
  Trigger calls scalar function doing heavy query per row
  Bulk 100K insert with complex AFTER trigger each row
  Audit trigger on table with 10K updates/sec — audit I/O bottleneck

DISASTER:
  Trigger updates same table (mutating table trigger — Oracle mutating table error)
  Recursive unguarded triggers
  External I/O in trigger

Bulk Load Bypass

sql
-- ETL: disable triggers temporarily (dangerous — needs governance)
ALTER TABLE payments DISABLE TRIGGER trg_payments_audit;
COPY payments FROM ...;
ALTER TABLE payments ENABLE TRIGGER trg_payments_audit;
-- PostgreSQL: COPY does not fire triggers unless DEFAULT used differently
-- Document: bulk load uses separate audit pipeline

Hibernate/JPA Interaction

text
session.saveAll(1000 entities):
  1000 INSERTs each firing triggers
  Alternative: audit via CDC — no per-row trigger on hot path
  updated_at: @UpdateTimestamp avoids trigger — but DBA SQL bypasses JPA

Measuring Trigger Cost

sql
-- PostgreSQL: pg_stat_user_tables, timing with/without trigger
-- Compare INSERT ... EXPLAIN ANALYZE with trigger disabled in test env
-- Oracle: SQL trace with trigger section
