Part 19 — Interview Questions

Junior

Q1: Source of truth for payment amount?

PostgreSQL payments/ledger service — not Redis, ES, or Mongo.

Q2: Why outbox pattern?

Atomic business write + event intent — avoid dual-write (L37).

Q3: Redis role?

Idempotency fast path, cache reference — not money SoR.

Q4: Read model lag acceptable where?

Payment list UI — not balance authorization.

Q5: Multi-AZ vs DR?

Multi-AZ same region HA; DR cross-region catastrophe (L40 vs L42).

Mid-Level

Q6: Design payment platform microservices data stores.

Postgres per service, outbox Kafka, read model, Redis idempotency, ES ops logs — reconcile.

Q7: When Mongo vs Postgres JSONB?

Same txn small metadata → JSONB; large blobs, separate scale → Mongo (L52).

Q8: When Cassandra vs Kafka-only?

Cassandra query by customer time window at scale; Kafka alone if consumers enough without random read.

Q9: Prevent N+1 on history API?

DTO projection or read model — not lazy entity graph (L48).

Q10: Idempotency dual layer?

Redis SET NX + Postgres UNIQUE — Redis performance, PG correctness (L53).

Senior

Q11: Tier 0 RPO/RTO architecture on AWS.

Aurora/RDS Multi-AZ sync, cross-region backup, warm DR, outbox, idempotent APIs, quarterly game day.

Q12: Strangler off Oracle monolith — data steps?

Extract payment Postgres, outbox events, saga ledger, stop cross-schema JOIN, CDC warehouse, deprecate XA.

Q13: Consistency catalog — three APIs examples.

POST strong, list eventual 5s, balance strong primary, ops ES disclaimer.

Staff / Solution Architect

Q14: Board asks “are we cloud resilient?” — evidence?

RTO/RTO matrix, last DR drill, backup restore proof, reconciliation green, Multi-AZ + cross-region, incident MTTR trends.

Q15: Evaluate adding Elasticsearch.

Ops LIKE pain, PCI redaction pipeline, ILM cost, not customer SoR, ADR, RBAC.

Scenario

Scenario: “CTO wants one database to simplify.”

Accept Postgres per bounded context minimum; unify ops with platform standards — not one shared schema — explain shared-DB microservice failure mode (L43).

Part 1 — Concept

What This Case Study Is

This lesson walks through a fictional but realistic retail + P2P payment platform—think consumer wallet + merchant checkout + person-to-person transfers—and shows how every persistence choice from Lessons 1–55 behaves together under normal load, Black Friday, and failure.

text
COMPANY: PayFlow Retail (fictional)
PRODUCTS:
  • Wallet checkout at online merchants
  • P2P send to phone/email
  • Branch/agent cash-in (optional)
SCALE (steady state):
  • 8M customers · 12M accounts · 180M payments/year
  • Peak: 3,500 captures/sec (Black Friday hour)
  • 40 microservice pods · 3 AWS regions (active-passive DR)

Part 2 — History

PayFlow’s Architecture Journey (Story Arc)

text
Year 1   Monolith PostgreSQL — 200 TPS — single team — Flyway + JPA
Year 2   Extract payment + ledger services — outbox introduced after dual-write incident
Year 3   P2P launches — cross-shard saga (L44) — Redis idempotency at API gateway
Year 4   Black Friday outage — read replica used for reports — primary pool exhausted (L32)
         → read model CQRS (L50) · connection pool fix · Hikari RDS Proxy
Year 5   Mongo metadata · Cassandra fraud events · OpenSearch for ops — polyglot mature
Year 6   Aurora Global DR · quarterly game days · consistency catalog mandatory (L56)
         Architect team owns selection matrix — feature teams own bounded schemas

Lesson: Each store was added after a measured pain, not on day one.

Part 3 — Problem Statement

Business Problems the Architecture Must Solve

Problem 1: Black Friday Peak

text
3,500 payment captures/sec for 2 hours
P2P spikes 2× normal — fraud rules need recent event window
Ops must search failures without touching OLTP

Problem 2: P2P Cross-Shard Transfer

text
Sender customer shard 2 · receiver shard 7
No global ACID — saga + compensations (L38, L44)
Idempotency on both API and saga steps

Problem 3: Merchant Disputes

text
Support needs trace_id timeline + authoritative Postgres payment row
Chargeback evidence — not ES totals

Problem 4: Regulatory Exam

text
Demonstrate RPO/RTO, backup restore, reconciliation, PII handling, 7-year retention

Problem 5: Cost Ceiling

text
CFO cap: infra + managed services ≤ $85k/month at steady state
Burst Black Friday ≤ 2.2× steady cost with auto-scale policy

Part 4 — Why This Exists

Why Walk Through One Integrated Story?

text
Isolated lessons teach mechanisms.
Case study teaches **trade-offs under pressure**:
  • Which store fails first?
  • What degrades gracefully?
  • What must never degrade?
  • Who owns the fix at 2 AM?

You are training for Solution Architect interviews and production ownership, not syntax quizzes.

Shard Model (Lesson 44)

text
8 PostgreSQL shard pairs (payment + ledger co-located by customer_id)
shard_id = hash(customer_id) % 8
Routing: Spring ShardContext + Hikari pool per shard in payment-api / ledger-api
P2P saga: debit shard A → credit shard B → compensate on failure

Core Tables (Per Shard — Payment DB)

text
payments · idempotency_records · outbox_events · saga_instances
Global (unsharded): flyway metadata, admin config small tables

Core Tables (Per Shard — Ledger DB)

text
accounts · ledger_entries  (account_id maps to same customer_id shard)

Part 8 — Execution Flow

Scenario A — Merchant Checkout (Single Shard)

text
1. Mobile app POST /payments Idempotency-Key + JWT customer_id
2. API Gateway Redis rate limit 30/min/customer (L53)
3. payment-api shard router → shard 3
4. Redis SET NX idempotency → Postgres INSERT payment PENDING + outbox
5. Response 202 { paymentId, status } from write txn
6. outbox-relay → Kafka PaymentCreated
7. ledger-consumer (same shard 3): debit wallet account, ledger_entries
8. Projectors: read model UPSERT; Mongo PSP metadata; Cassandra event; ES log line
9. Customer list screen (eventual): read model ≤ 3s lag SLA
10. Balance widget: ledger-api primary read — strong

SQL count target capture path: ≤ 5 statements (L47 budget).

Scenario B — P2P Transfer (Cross Shard)

text
1. POST /p2p/transfers — idempotency key global
2. Saga orchestrator (payment-api) saga_id assigned
3. Step 1 @Transactional shard 2: debit sender account, outbox P2PDebited
4. Step 2 @Transactional shard 7: credit receiver, outbox P2PCredited
5. If step 2 fails: compensate step 1 credit back shard 2
6. processed_events idempotency on each Kafka consumer step
7. Reconciliation hourly: SUM debits = SUM credits for saga_type P2P

No XA (L39). Latency p99 ~ 180ms vs ~ 45ms single-shard checkout.

Scenario C — Black Friday Hour 0

text
T-0  Traffic 800/sec → 2,200/sec in 10 min
     HPA payment-api 40 → 80 pods (CPU 60% target)
     RDS Proxy absorbs connection multiplexing
     Redis coord CPU 55% — no eviction events
     Kafka lag payment-events 2s → 8s → back to 3s after consumer scale
     Read model lag p99 4s — within SLA
     OpenSearch indexing delay 30s — ops acceptable

T+45 min Spike 3,500/sec
     One shard hot (merchant campaign customer cluster) — shard 5 CPU 88%
     Action: route mega-merchant customers to dedicated shard 8 (pre-planned)
     Cassandra fraud reads LOCAL_QUORUM p99 12ms
     Postgres capture p99 95ms — within 200ms SLO

T+2 hr Cooldown
     Scale down consumers gradually; keep ES extra nodes 24h for incident search

Scenario D — Incident: Primary Shard Failover

text
14:22 shard 3 Aurora writer failure
14:23 automatic failover to standby AZ — 47s
14:24 connection pool retry storm — circuit breaker opens 30s
14:25 traffic resumes — idempotent retries safe
14:40 post-incident: 23 in-flight txns rolled back — clients retry — no duplicate charges
OpenSearch trace investigation for timeout errors
Reconciliation job: zero amount drift shard 3 for incident window

Part 11 — Code / SQL Examples

PayFlow Standards (Representative)

Capture with Shard + Idempotency

java
@Service
@RequiredArgsConstructor
public class PayFlowCaptureService {

    private final ShardRouter router;
    private final RedisIdempotencyService redisIdempotency;
    private final PaymentRepository paymentRepo;
    private final OutboxEventRepository outboxRepo;

    @RequiresShard
    @Transactional
    public PaymentResult capture(UUID customerId, CaptureCommand cmd) {
        router.bind(customerId);

        redisIdempotency.begin(cmd.key(), cmd.hash(), Duration.ofHours(24))
            .ifPresent(r -> { throw new IdempotentReplayException(r); });

        Payment p = paymentRepo.save(Payment.pending(customerId, cmd));
        outboxRepo.save(OutboxEvent.paymentCreated(p));

        PaymentResult result = PaymentResult.from(p);
        redisIdempotency.complete(cmd.key(), result, Duration.ofHours(24));
        return result;
    }
}

P2P Saga Orchestrator (Simplified)

java
public void p2pTransfer(P2PCommand cmd) {
    UUID sagaId = UUID.randomUUID();
    sagaRepo.start(sagaId, "P2P", cmd);

    try {
        debitSender(cmd, sagaId);   // shard A — local @Transactional
        creditReceiver(cmd, sagaId); // shard B — local @Transactional
        sagaRepo.complete(sagaId);
    } catch (Exception ex) {
        compensateDebit(cmd, sagaId);
        sagaRepo.fail(sagaId);
        throw ex;
    }
}

Black Friday Reconciliation (Run Every Hour During Event)

sql
-- Shard-agnostic job (runs per shard + aggregate)
SELECT shard_id,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'CAPTURED') AS captured_count,
       SUM(amount) FILTER (WHERE status = 'CAPTURED') AS captured_total
FROM payments
WHERE created_at >= NOW() - INTERVAL '1 hour'
GROUP BY shard_id;

-- Cross-system drift (read model)
SELECT COUNT(*) AS missing
FROM payments p
LEFT JOIN payment_list_view r ON r.payment_id = p.payment_id
WHERE p.created_at >= NOW() - INTERVAL '1 hour'
  AND r.payment_id IS NULL;

Part 18 — Common Mistakes

War Story 1 — “Black Friday Read Replica”

text
Ops pointed BI at replica · replica lag + heavy scan · capture pool starved indirectly
Fix: CQRS read DB + warehouse — never ad-hoc replica reports during peak

War Story 2 — “Mongo Balance Cache”

text
Growth hack cached balance in Redis for home screen · stale after P2P · viral tweet outrage
Fix: balance always ledger primary · cache only branch metadata

War Story 3 — “ES Refund Total”

text
Finance used Kibana aggregation for refund sum · missing docs · $400k reporting error
Fix: Snowflake official numbers · ES investigation only

War Story 4 — “Mega Merchant Hot Shard”

text
One merchant 40% traffic on shard 5 · designed isolation shard 8 pre-allocated

War Story 5 — “Saga Without Idempotent Consumer”

text
P2P duplicate credit on Kafka redelivery · processed_events table added · hourly reconcile

Part 19 — Interview Questions

Junior

Q1: PayFlow money SoR?

PostgreSQL ledger + payments shards — authoritative.

Q2: Why 8 shards?

Write scale + fault isolation — customer_id hash — co-locate payment + ledger.

Q3: P2P cross-shard without 2PC?

Saga debit → credit → compensate — idempotent steps.

Q4: Black Friday read list lag OK?

Yes if ≤5s SLA documented — not for balance.

Q5: Redis down impact?

Slower idempotency via Postgres — capture continues.

Mid-Level

Q6: Walk through merchant checkout data flow.

Redis NX → PG payment+outbox → Kafka → ledger → projectors read/mongo/cass/ES.

Q7: Reconciliation during Black Friday hourly?

Per-shard captured totals vs ledger vs read model missing count.

Q8: Hot shard mitigation?

Dedicated merchant shard, rate limits, pre-scale, customer_id salt last resort.

Q9: Why Cassandra for fraud not PG?

18k events/sec peak — time-window queries — not money SoR.

Q10: OpenSearch role in dispute?

trace timeline — Postgres confirms amount/status.

Senior

Q11: Design PayFlow from scratch for 3,500/sec — components?

8 Aurora shards, RDS Proxy, Redis coord, Kafka outbox, read model, optional Cass+ES, reconcile, DR.

Q12: Kafka down policy?

ADR: capture continues until outbox depth threshold then read-only mode — document RPO event lag.

Q13: Cost optimize $85k cap?

Right-size replicas, ILM ES, Cassandra TTL, Snowflake warehouse auto-suspend, avoid over-sharding early.

Staff / Solution Architect

Q14: Regulator asks resilience evidence — what do you show?

L56 pack + PayFlow game day results + reconciliation + backup restore + consistency catalog.

Q15: Acquire bank legacy Oracle — integrate PayFlow?

CDC strangler, parallel run reconcile, no big-bang, keep Oracle Tier 0 until cutover sign-off.

Scenario

Scenario: “Black Friday: list shows paid but balance unchanged for 30s.”

Ledger consumer lag or saga incomplete — check Kafka lag, saga_instances, not read model alone — Postgres ledger balance is truth for support script.

Part 1 — Concept

What This Case Study Covers

Cross-border and B2B corporate payments differ sharply from retail P2P (Lesson 57). Money moves in multiple currencies, through nostro/vostro correspondent relationships, with cut-off windows, compliance holds, and settlement cycles that can take seconds to days.

text
RETAIL P2P (Lesson 57)              CROSS-BORDER B2B (Lesson 58)
──────────────────────              ────────────────────────────
Single currency wallet common       Multi-currency mandatory
Instant debit/credit UX             Cut-off + settlement date (T+0/T+1/T+2)
Consumer idempotency                Invoice + PO + approval workflows
Simple saga 2 accounts              FX quote → hold → SWIFT/ISO20022 rail
Low compliance latency OK seconds   Sanctions screening holds minutes–hours
One ledger per customer             Corporate hierarchy + nostro pools

Fictional Company: CorpPay Global

text
PRODUCTS:
  • B2B supplier payments (AP) — USD/EUR/GBP/INR corridors
  • Cross-border wire via SWIFT / local rails (SEPA, FPS, IMPS)
  • FX conversion with locked quote snapshot
  • Treasury nostro reconciliation

SCALE:
  • 12,000 corporate clients · 80k users
  • 25M payments/year · avg ticket $8,400 (vs $47 retail)
  • Peak: 450 B2B payments/min (batch windows 09:00–11:00 ET)
  • 95% payments require compliance screening record

Part 2 — History

How CorpPay’s Data Model Diverged from Retail

text
Year 1   Forked PayFlow ledger — added currency_code everywhere (L43)
Year 2   FX desk integration — quote snapshot table — never recompute rate at settlement
Year 3   Sanctions hold state machine — payments PENDING_COMPLIANCE for 4% volume
Year 4   Nostro statement import — reconciliation mismatch $2.1M caught — new nostro_ledger
Year 5   ISO 20022 pain.001/pain.002 stored Mongo + canonical row Postgres
Year 6   Cut-off engine — timezone-aware — missed cut-off saga compensation standard
         Separate B2B schema — NOT shared DB with retail wallet (regulatory boundary)

Architect decision: Corporate and retail different bounded contexts, optionally same platform team, never same payment table.

Part 3 — Problem Statement

B2B / Cross-Border Problems Data Must Solve

Problem 1: FX Rate Integrity

text
Quote USD/EUR = 0.92134 at 10:00:00 — settle at 14:00 — rate moved
Must store **locked quote snapshot** — not live FX on settlement row
Regulator asks: prove rate applied to corporate payment X

Problem 2: Multi-Currency Ledger Without Silent Conversion

text
USD account debited $10,000 — beneficiary receives EUR — two currency truths
Double-entry in **each currency leg** + **FX bridge entries** (Lesson 43 extended)
Never `SUM(amount)` across mixed currencies without FX snapshot

Problem 3: Compliance Holds

text
Sanctions hit → payment frozen days — status PENDING_COMPLIANCE — audit trail immutable
Release or reject — compensating entries — not DELETE

Problem 4: Cut-Off Windows

text
SWIFT correspondent cut-off 17:00 EST — submit 17:01 → value date T+1
Architecture must model **value_date**, **cutoff_corridor**, **rail_type**

Problem 5: Nostro / Vostro Reconciliation

text
Our USD nostro at Bank X statement ≠ internal nostro_ledger — treasury incident
Separate reconciliation tier — not customer payment capture path

Part 4 — Why This Exists

Why Not Extend PayFlow As-Is?

FactorRetailB2B Cross-border
WorkflowSingle step captureMulti-step approval + batch
Data volume/secVery high small ticketsLower count, larger payload
Consistency UXInstantSettlement date explicit
SchemaSimple payment rowInvoice refs, FX legs, nostro
ComplianceBasic AML velocitySanctions lists, PEP, trade finance
ReportingDaily aggregatesRegulatory nostro + FX exposure

CorpPay runs separate microservices and PostgreSQL databases from PayFlow retail, shared platform (Kafka, Redis, OpenSearch) only.

│ rail-adapters    │ Mongo               │ iso20022_messages, swift_ack_nack      │
│ payment-query    │ PG payment_read_b2b │ corporate_payment_list_view            │
│ warehouse        │ Snowflake           │ regulatory FX + nostro reports         │
└──────────────────┴─────────────────────┴────────────────────────────────────────┘

Payment State Machine (B2B — Richer Than Retail)

text
DRAFT → PENDING_APPROVAL → APPROVED → FX_QUOTED → COMPLIANCE_SCREENING
  → PENDING_COMPLIANCE (hold) → RELEASED → SUBMITTED_TO_RAIL
  → IN_TRANSIT → SETTLED → RECONCILED
Branches: REJECTED · CANCELLED · RETURNED · FAILED (each with ledger reversal)

Multi-Leg Payment Model

text
One logical payment_id:
  Leg 1: DEBIT corporate USD account  $10,000
  Leg 2: FX bridge entries (USD→EUR at quoted rate)
  Leg 3: CREDIT beneficiary EUR nostro/vostro routing
Each leg: currency_code, amount, ledger_entry_ids[], value_date

Part 6 — Storage Internals

FX Quote Snapshot (Immutable)

sql
CREATE TABLE fx_quotes (
    quote_id          UUID PRIMARY KEY,
    payment_id        UUID NOT NULL,
    base_currency     CHAR(3) NOT NULL,
    quote_currency    CHAR(3) NOT NULL,
    rate              DECIMAL(18,8) NOT NULL,
    inverse_rate      DECIMAL(18,8) NOT NULL,
    base_amount       DECIMAL(19,4) NOT NULL,
    quote_amount      DECIMAL(19,4) NOT NULL,
    rate_source       VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,   -- ECB, REUTERS, DESK
    valid_until       TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
    locked_at         TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
    created_at        TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);

-- Payment references quote_id — settlement uses snapshot ONLY
ALTER TABLE payments_b2b ADD COLUMN fx_quote_id UUID REFERENCES fx_quotes(quote_id);

Rule: No UPDATE rate on fx_quotes — new quote = new row.

Multi-Currency Ledger Entries

sql
CREATE TABLE ledger_entries (
    entry_id        UUID PRIMARY KEY,
    account_id      UUID NOT NULL,
    payment_id      UUID NOT NULL,
    leg_type        VARCHAR(30) NOT NULL,  -- DEBIT, CREDIT, FX_GAIN, FX_LOSS
    direction       CHAR(6) NOT NULL CHECK (direction IN ('DEBIT','CREDIT')),
    amount          DECIMAL(19,4) NOT NULL CHECK (amount > 0),
    currency_code   CHAR(3) NOT NULL,
    value_date      DATE NOT NULL,
    balance_after   DECIMAL(19,4) NOT NULL,
    correlation_id  UUID NOT NULL,
    created_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);

CREATE INDEX ix_ledger_account_ccy_date
    ON ledger_entries (account_id, currency_code, value_date DESC);

Nostro Sub-Ledger (Treasury)

sql
CREATE TABLE nostro_accounts (
    nostro_account_id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
    bank_bic          VARCHAR(11) NOT NULL,
    currency_code     CHAR(3) NOT NULL,
    account_number    VARCHAR(34) NOT NULL,
    ledger_balance    DECIMAL(19,4) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    statement_balance DECIMAL(19,4),  -- last import
    last_statement_at TIMESTAMPTZ
);

CREATE TABLE nostro_entries (
    entry_id          UUID PRIMARY KEY,
    nostro_account_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES nostro_accounts(nostro_account_id),
    payment_id        UUID,
    entry_type        VARCHAR(30) NOT NULL,
    amount            DECIMAL(19,4) NOT NULL,
    currency_code     CHAR(3) NOT NULL,
    value_date        DATE NOT NULL,
    swift_ref         VARCHAR(50),
    created_at        TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);

Compliance Hold

sql
CREATE TABLE compliance_holds (
    hold_id       UUID PRIMARY KEY,
    payment_id    UUID NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    case_status   VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,  -- OPEN, RELEASED, REJECTED
    screening_ref VARCHAR(100),
    reason_code   VARCHAR(50),
    opened_at     TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
    closed_at     TIMESTAMPTZ,
    decision_by   VARCHAR(100)
);

-- payments_b2b.status = PENDING_COMPLIANCE while hold OPEN
-- NEVER DELETE hold row — audit

Part 7 — Memory Usage

B2B Workload Profile vs Retail

AspectRetail PayFlow (L57)CorpPay B2B
TPS peak3,500/sec~8/sec avg, 450/min batch peak
Row widthNarrowWide (invoice, legs, quote refs)
Txn duration<200msSeconds (approval) to days (hold)
Long-running stateRareCommon — compliance holds
JPA persistence ctxShortLong workflows — state machine not long @Transactional
Mongo payloadWebhook KBISO20022 XML MB — S3 pointer for large

Insight: B2B stresses schema correctness, audit, and state machines more than raw TPS. Connection pools smaller; workflow tables grow large.

Part 8 — Execution Flow

Flow A — USD→EUR Supplier Payment (Happy Path)

text
1. Corporate user creates payment DRAFT — invoice refs, beneficiary, USD $10,000
2. Approval workflow → APPROVED (separate rows approval_steps)
3. fx-service: lock quote quote_id — EUR 9,213.40 @ 0.92134 — valid 30 min
4. payment-orchestrator @Transactional:
     INSERT payments_b2b SETTLEMENT_PENDING
     INSERT fx_quotes link
     INSERT outbox PaymentFxQuoted
5. compliance-svc: screen — PASS — INSERT compliance_holds RELEASED immediately
6. Ledger saga (same currency legs sequenced):
     a. DEBIT corporate USD account $10,000 (value_date T)
     b. FX bridge entries USD/EUR per quote snapshot
     c. CREDIT outbound EUR nostro pool €9,213.40 (value_date T)
7. rail-adapter: build pain.001 → Mongo store + Kafka to SWIFT gateway
8. ACK received → status IN_TRANSIT → outbox
9. MT910/statement line matched → SETTLED → nostro_entries reconcile
10. Corporate query API: list view eventual; detail shows quote snapshot immutable

Cut-Off Miss Flow

text
17:02 submission for SWIFT cut-off 17:00:
  Engine sets value_date T+1, status SUBMITTED_TO_RAIL
  Corporate UI: "Value date next business day"
  No re-debit — funds remain in outbound nostro pool leg with T+1 value_date
  Saga does NOT reverse FX quote — quote re-validated or re-quoted next morning per policy

Compliance Hold Flow

text
Screening MATCH potential sanctions:
  payments_b2b → PENDING_COMPLIANCE
  compliance_holds OPEN — ledger debit may be ON_HOLD entry (separate hold account)
  Analyst RELEASED → continue rail submission
  OR REJECTED → reversal ledger entries + status REJECTED + outbox PaymentRejected
  OpenSearch case timeline + Postgres hold row authoritative

FX Quote Lock (JPA + Immutable Entity)

java
@Entity

@Immutable
public class FxQuote {
    @Id
    private UUID quoteId;
    private UUID paymentId;
    private String baseCurrency;
    private String quoteCurrency;

Payment Orchestrator — Quote Then Compliance

java
@Transactional
public PaymentSubmitResult submitApprovedPayment(UUID paymentId) {
    PaymentB2B payment = paymentRepo.findById(paymentId).orElseThrow();
    assertStatus(payment, APPROVED);

    FxQuote quote = fxService.lockQuote(payment);  // inserts fx_quotes row
    payment.setFxQuoteId(quote.getQuoteId());
    payment.setStatus(FX_QUOTED);

    outboxRepo.save(OutboxEvent.fxQuoted(payment, quote));

    payment.setStatus(COMPLIANCE_SCREENING);
    paymentRepo.save(payment);
    outboxRepo.save(OutboxEvent.complianceRequested(payment));

    return PaymentSubmitResult.quoted(payment, quote);
}
// compliance consumer continues async — NOT blocking HTTP thread days

Multi-Currency Ledger Posting

java
@Transactional
public void postSettlementLegs(PaymentB2B payment, FxQuote quote) {
    Account usdAccount = accountRepo.findCorporateFunding(payment.getCorporateId(), "USD");
    postDebit(usdAccount, payment.getBaseAmount(), "USD", payment.getValueDate());

    postFxBridge(payment, quote);  // balanced USD/EUR internal accounts

    NostroPool eurPool = nostroRepo.findOutboundPool("EUR");
    postCredit(eurPool, quote.getQuoteAmount(), "EUR", payment.getValueDate());
}

Nostro Reconciliation SQL

sql
-- Internal nostro ledger vs statement import line
SELECT
    n.nostro_account_id,
    n.currency_code,
    n.ledger_balance AS internal_balance,
    n.statement_balance AS bank_statement_balance,
    n.ledger_balance - n.statement_balance AS variance
FROM nostro_accounts n
WHERE ABS(n.ledger_balance - COALESCE(n.statement_balance, n.ledger_balance)) > 0.01;

-- Unmatched SWIFT refs
SELECT ne.entry_id, ne.swift_ref, ne.amount, ne.currency_code
FROM nostro_entries ne
LEFT JOIN statement_lines sl ON sl.swift_ref = ne.swift_ref
WHERE sl.swift_ref IS NULL
  AND ne.value_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '7 days';

Cut-Off Engine

java
public ValueDateResult applyCutoff(PaymentB2B payment, Instant submitTime, ZoneId corridorZone) {
    CutoffSchedule schedule = cutoffRepo.find(payment.getRailType(), payment.getCurrencyCorridor());
    ZonedDateTime submit = submitTime.atZone(corridorZone);
    if (submit.isAfter(schedule.getTodayCutoff())) {
        return ValueDateResult.nextBusinessDay(schedule.nextBusinessDate());
    }
    return ValueDateResult.sameDay(submit.toLocalDate());
}

Part 12 — Production Usage

CorpPay Operating Model

Batch Windows

text
09:00–11:00 ET — AP batch approval surge — scale payment-orchestrator pods ×2
17:00 ET — SWIFT cut-off — alert if outbox lag > 30s after 16:45
End-of-day — treasury nostro recon job — blocks CFO dashboard until variance = 0

Compliance Operations

text
compliance_holds OPEN queue in PG — Kibana supplements message search
SLA: 95% screens < 60s auto; manual cases < 4 business hours
Every RELEASED/REJECTED writes compliance_audit immutable table

Data Residency

text
EU corporates: PG cluster eu-west — Mongo ES EU — sanctions list EU storage
US treasury nostro: us-east PG — cross-border replication **not** for PII — legal review
Architect maps **data residency** per corporate entity — not one global shard (contrast L57 hash shard)

Retention

text
fx_quotes, ledger_entries, compliance_holds: 7+ years
ISO20022 Mongo: 7 years or S3 archive with index doc
Sanctions screening raw response: 5 years encrypted

State Machine — Avoid Long @Transactional

java
// ❌ @Transactional spanning approval days
// ✅ Each transition one txn + outbox event
@Transactional
public void releaseComplianceHold(UUID holdId, ComplianceDecision decision) {
    ComplianceHold hold = holdRepo.findById(holdId).orElseThrow();
    hold.close(decision);
    PaymentB2B payment = paymentRepo.findById(hold.getPaymentId()).orElseThrow();
    payment.setStatus(RELEASED);
    outboxRepo.save(OutboxEvent.complianceReleased(payment));
}

Wide Payment Entity vs Projections

Multi-Currency Money Embeddable

java
@Embeddable
public record Money(@Column(precision=19,scale=4) BigDecimal amount,
                    @Column(length=3) String currencyCode) {
    public void assertSameCurrency(Money other) {

            throw new CurrencyMismatchException();
    }
}

Part 18 — Common Mistakes

Mistake 1: Single Currency Ledger Assumption

text
Reporting "total ledger balance $50M" mixing EUR and USD — CFO false number

Mistake 2: Re-Reading FX Rate at Settlement

text
Rate moved — corporate dispute — regulatory finding — always quote_id snapshot

Mistake 3: Compliance DELETE

text
DELETE payment on reject — audit fail — status REJECTED + reversal entries

Mistake 4: Retail Sharding on corporate_id Without Residency

text
EU data in US shard — GDPR violation — region-first routing

Mistake 5: Long HTTP Wait for Compliance

text
Thread blocked 48 hours — pool exhaustion — async hold + webhook to corporate

Mistake 6: Nostro = Sum of Customer Balances

text
Treasury pool ≠ customer liabilities — separate ledgers

Part 19 — Interview Questions

Junior

Q1: Why separate B2B database from retail?

Different workflows, compliance, FX, amounts, regulatory boundaries.

Q2: FX quote snapshot purpose?

Prove locked rate at payment time — settlement uses quote_id not live rate.

Q3: PENDING_COMPLIANCE meaning?

Sanctions/AML hold — funds blocked — audit trail until RELEASED/REJECTED.

Q4: value_date vs created_at?

value_date = settlement/cut-off business date; created_at = system timestamp.

Q5: Nostro account?

Our currency account at correspondent bank — treasury reconciliation.

Mid-Level

Q6: Multi-currency ledger posting for USD→EUR wire?

Debit USD corporate, FX bridge at snapshot, credit EUR nostro pool — balanced per currency.

Q7: Cut-off missed handling?

value_date T+1, UI messaging, no silent same-day assumption, re-quote policy.

Q8: B2B idempotency vs retail?

corporate_id + client_payment_reference UNIQUE; large wire resubmit protection.

Q9: ISO20022 in Mongo vs Postgres?

Large XML Mongo/S3; canonical status/amounts Postgres SoR.

Q10: Compliance release flow?

Close hold row, update payment status, outbox continue rail, ledger move from HOLD if used.

Senior

Q11: Design CorpPay cross-border architecture.

Separate PG services, fx_quotes immutable, compliance async, nostro treasury, Mongo ISO, read model, Snowflake regulatory, no 2PC.

Q12: Retail vs B2B sharding strategy?

Retail customer_id hash TPS; B2B region residency + corporate_id — lower TPS wider rows.

Q13: Nostro variance $2.1M incident response?

Stop submissions, compare nostro_entries vs statement_lines, SWIFT ref match, treasury war room, not customer API.

Staff / Architect

Q14: Acquire bank with Oracle trade finance — integrate CorpPay?

CDC strangler, parallel FX/hold models, nostro mapping, 12-month cutover reconcile.

Q15: Data residency for multi-region corporates?

Entity-region mapping drives PG cluster routing — consistency catalog per jurisdiction.

Scenario

Scenario: "Corporate paid invoice twice same reference."

Check UNIQUE (corporate_id, client_payment_reference) — idempotency return second — if missing constraint, reconciliation + compensating reversal wire.

Part 1 — Concept

What Is Compliance Data Architecture?

AML (Anti–Money Laundering), sanctions screening, and regulatory reporting require specialized data pipelines that link to payments but must never become the payment ledger. Compliance systems observe, hold, enrich, and report — they do not authorize money movement alone.

text
PAYMENT LEDGER (Tier 0)                 COMPLIANCE LAYER (Tier 1–2)
───────────────────────                 ─────────────────────────────
Postgres: payments, accounts          Postgres: screening_cases, holds
Authoritative: amount, status           Watchlists: sanctions PEP lists
Capture saga completes debit            Screening: match scores, decisions
                                        Reporting: STR/SAR, CTR marts (warehouse)
        │                                        ▲
        └──── events / CDC / API ────────────────┘
              (read-only influence via HOLD status)

Key Terms

TermMeaning
AMLDetect suspicious patterns — ongoing monitoring
Sanctions screeningMatch payer/beneficiary against OFAC/EU/UN lists
PEPPolitically Exposed Person — enhanced due diligence
KYCKnow Your Customer — identity at onboarding
STR/SARSuspicious Transaction Report — filed to FIU/regulator
CTRCurrency Transaction Report — large cash thresholds (jurisdiction-specific)
WatchlistSanctions/PEP/adverse media reference data
Case managementAnalyst workflow OPEN → INVESTIGATING → CLOSED

Golden Rule

Compliance data explains and reports on payments; Postgres ledger + ledger-service authorize settlement. A screening “FAIL” becomes a hold on payment status — not a parallel balance.

Part 2 — History

Evolution of Compliance Data in Payment Platforms

text
1990s   Batch sanctions files overnight — mainframe match — payments delayed 24h
2000s   Real-time OFAC on wire entry — Oracle staging tables
2010s   Vendor APIs (Refinitiv, Dow Jones, ComplyAdvantage) — JSON responses stored
2015+   Kafka streaming rules — velocity checks Cassandra (L54) — Postgres holds
2018    GDPR + data minimization — PII segregation — tokenized screening keys
2020+   ISO20022 enriched remittance data — more fields to screen
        Warehouse marts for regulatory returns (COREP, FINTRAC, RBI-style filings)
2024+   AI-assisted alert scoring — model features in warehouse — human decision auditable
        Architects document **compliance boundary** in same tier map as L56

Historical Lesson

Regulators punish gaps in audit trail and report accuracy, not whether you used Mongo or Snowflake. Architecture must prove what was known when, who decided, and that payment SoR was unchanged except via formal hold/release.

Part 3 — Problem Statement

What Problems Does Compliance Data Architecture Solve?

Problem 1: Real-Time Screening Without Blocking OLTP

text
10,000 retail captures/sec — cannot call vendor API synchronously on every txn
Tier: async screening + risk-based sync for high-value B2B (L58)

Problem 2: Watchlist Freshness

text
OFAC list updated 14:00 — payment at 14:05 must use current list version
Store **list_version_id** on every screening result

Problem 3: False Positive Workflow

text
"AHMED KHAN" matches sanctions — analyst clears — decision must persist — re-screen must not re-alert blindly

Problem 4: STR/SAR Filing Evidence

text
Analyst files STR — must bundle transactions, notes, screening snapshots — immutable filing package

Problem 5: Separation from Ledger

text
Compliance team queries wide PII — payment API must not expose sanctions raw hits to merchants

Part 4 — Why This Exists

Why Not Columns on payments Table?

text
payments table grows 40 compliance columns — coupling — migrations break capture path
Analyst notes, attachments, watchlist match JSON — wrong shape for OLTP row
Retention differs: screening vendor response 5yr — payment 7yr — legal hold varies
Access RBAC: fraud analysts ≠ payment engineers — separate DB/schema/service
Performance: screening search OpenSearch — not Postgres seq scan on message fields

Pattern: payment_id correlation UUID across compliance DB, warehouse, ES — no FK cross-service (L43).

Screening Pipeline (Async — Retail Scale)

text
1. payment-service COMMIT capture (Tier 0)
2. outbox PaymentCreated → Kafka
3. screening-consumer:
     a. Load payment snapshot fields (amount, customer, counterparty token)
     b. watchlist_version = current OFAC/EU bundle id
     c. Vendor API or local inverted index match
     d. INSERT screening_results (payment_id, list_version, match_score, raw_ref)
     e. If score > threshold → INSERT compliance_holds OPEN
        → API call payment-service: transition PENDING_COMPLIANCE (saga command)
     f. Else INSERT screening_results CLEAR
4. payment remains CAPTURED for retail wallet if policy = post-capture screen
   OR blocked before rail if B2B policy (L58) — **policy per product in consistency catalog**

Hold → Release → Ledger (CorpPay B2B)

text
Payment PENDING_COMPLIANCE:
  Ledger may use HOLD account segregation (L58) — funds not in outbound pool
Analyst RELEASED:
  compliance_cases decision row immutable
  outbox ComplianceReleased → payment-orchestrator continues rail saga
Analyst REJECTED:
  Reversal ledger entries — payment REJECTED — STR optional if suspicious

Transaction Monitoring (Batch)

text
Nightly Snowflake job:
  Detect structuring: 9,900 USD × 15 txns same week same customer (avoid 10k CTR)
  Detect velocity: 50 P2P to new beneficiaries 24h
  Output: aml_alerts table → cases OPEN — not auto-debit
Human review mandatory before filing STR

Part 6 — Storage Internals

Schema — Compliance PostgreSQL (compliance_db)

Screening Result (Immutable)

sql
CREATE TABLE screening_results (
    screening_id      UUID PRIMARY KEY,
    payment_id          UUID NOT NULL,
    customer_id         UUID NOT NULL,
    beneficiary_token   VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL,  -- tokenized, not raw name in hot path
    list_version_id     UUID NOT NULL,
    screening_type      VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,   -- SANCTIONS, PEP, ADVERSE_MEDIA
    match_score         DECIMAL(5,2),
    match_status        VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,   -- CLEAR, POTENTIAL_MATCH, CONFIRMED
    vendor_ref          VARCHAR(100),
    screened_at         TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    raw_response_ref    VARCHAR(255)            -- S3 or Mongo pointer — not inline PAN/PII
);

CREATE INDEX ix_screening_payment ON screening_results (payment_id);
CREATE INDEX ix_screening_status_time ON screening_results (match_status, screened_at);

Watchlist Version

sql
CREATE TABLE watchlist_versions (
    list_version_id   UUID PRIMARY KEY,
    list_source       VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,   -- OFAC_SDN, EU_CONS, UN, INTERNAL
    effective_from    TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
    effective_to      TIMESTAMPTZ,
    record_count      BIGINT NOT NULL,
    ingestion_job_id  UUID NOT NULL,
    checksum_sha256   CHAR(64) NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE watchlist_entries (
    entry_id          UUID PRIMARY KEY,
    list_version_id   UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES watchlist_versions(list_version_id),
    primary_name      TEXT NOT NULL,
    aliases           TEXT[],
    entity_type       VARCHAR(20),
    country_code      CHAR(2),
    source_record_id  VARCHAR(100)
);

CREATE INDEX ix_watchlist_name_trgm ON watchlist_entries USING gin (primary_name gin_trgm_ops);
-- Or push to OpenSearch for fuzzy match — PG for exact admin

Case Management

sql
CREATE TABLE compliance_cases (
    case_id           UUID PRIMARY KEY,
    case_type         VARCHAR(30) NOT NULL,   -- SANCTIONS_HIT, TM_ALERT, MANUAL_REVIEW
    payment_id        UUID,
    customer_id       UUID NOT NULL,
    status            VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,   -- OPEN, INVESTIGATING, ESCALATED, CLOSED
    priority          VARCHAR(10) NOT NULL,
    assigned_to       VARCHAR(100),
    opened_at         TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
    closed_at         TIMESTAMPTZ,
    disposition       VARCHAR(30),              -- FALSE_POSITIVE, TRUE_MATCH, SAR_FILED
    version           BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0
);

CREATE TABLE case_decisions (
    decision_id       UUID PRIMARY KEY,
    case_id           UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES compliance_cases(case_id),
    decision          VARCHAR(30) NOT NULL,
    rationale         TEXT NOT NULL,
    decided_by        VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
    decided_at        TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);
-- INSERT-only for decisions — no UPDATE rationale

STR/SAR Filing Package

sql
CREATE TABLE regulatory_filings (
    filing_id         UUID PRIMARY KEY,
    filing_type       VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,   -- STR, SAR, CTR
    jurisdiction      CHAR(2) NOT NULL,
    case_id           UUID NOT NULL,
    status            VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,   -- DRAFT, SUBMITTED, ACKNOWLEDGED
    submitted_at      TIMESTAMPTZ,
    regulator_ref     VARCHAR(100),
    package_ref       VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,  -- S3 immutable WORM object
    created_at        TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);

CREATE TABLE filing_transactions (
    filing_id         UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES regulatory_filings(filing_id),
    payment_id        UUID NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (filing_id, payment_id)
);

Link to Payment — No Ledger Columns

text
payments_b2b.status updated ONLY via payment-service command API
compliance-service NEVER UPDATE accounts.balance
Correlation: payment_id UUID in all compliance tables

Part 8 — Execution Flow

End-to-End Flows

Flow A — Retail Post-Capture Screen (PayFlow L57)

text
1. Capture COMMIT — payment CAPTURED — customer sees success (product policy)
2. screening-consumer screens within 30s
3. CLEAR → no action
4. POTENTIAL_MATCH → case OPEN — payment flagged internally — optional wallet limit freeze via separate limit-service (not ledger rewrite)
5. CONFIRMED sanctions → escalate — account suspension saga — regulator timeline hours

Flow B — B2B Pre-Rail Hold (CorpPay L58)

text
1. Payment APPROVED → FX quoted
2. Sync sanctions screen before ledger debit (high value)
3. HOLD → PENDING_COMPLIANCE — ledger HOLD account movement
4. Analyst FALSE_POSITIVE → RELEASED → continue settlement saga
5. TRUE_MATCH → REJECTED + reversal + STR draft case

Flow C — Transaction Monitoring → STR

text
1. Snowflake detects structuring pattern — INSERT aml_alerts
2. Case management OPEN — analyst 3-day investigation
3. Links 15 payments via payment_id list
4. Decision SAR_FILED → regulatory_filings SUBMITTED
5. filing-gateway writes WORM package to S3 — checksum in PG
6. Payment rows unchanged except case disposition flags — ledger already settled — STR is reporting not reversal (unless separate freeze action)

Flow D — Watchlist Update Intraday

text
1. OFAC emergency append — ingestion job list_version_id new
2. Publish WatchlistUpdated event
3. Rescreen open payments last 24h batch job — screening_results new rows — version pinned
4. Re-open cases if new match on previously CLEAR (policy-driven)

Flow E — CDC to Warehouse (Regulatory Mart)

text
1. Debezium payments + ledger + screening_results → Kafka
2. Snowflake merge fact_payments, fact_screenings, dim_watchlist_version
3. Monthly regulatory return generated from mart — not from OpenSearch
4. Reconcile mart totals to Postgres reconciliation job (L56)

Part 11 — Code / SQL Examples

Screening Consumer (Spring)

java
@KafkaListener(topics = "payment-events")
@Transactional("complianceTransactionManager")
public void onPaymentCreated(PaymentCreatedEvent event) {
    if (screeningResultRepo.existsByPaymentIdAndType(event.paymentId(), SANCTIONS)) {
        return; // idempotent
    }

    WatchlistVersion version = watchlistService.currentVersion(OFAC_SDN);
    ScreeningResult result = screeningEngine.screen(event, version);

    screeningResultRepo.save(result);

    if (result.requiresHold()) {
        complianceCaseService.openSanctionsCase(event, result);
        paymentCommandClient.markPendingCompliance(event.paymentId());
    }
}

Payment Command Client (Boundary — Not SQL Join)

java
@Component
public class PaymentCommandClient {
    public void markPendingCompliance(UUID paymentId) {
        restClient.post()
            .uri("/internal/payments/{id}/compliance-hold", paymentId)
            .retrieve()
            .toBodilessEntity();
        // payment-service owns status transition + outbox PaymentComplianceHold
    }
}

STR Filing Package Job

sql
-- Payments linked to case for filing bundle
SELECT p.payment_id, p.amount, p.currency_code, p.created_at, p.status,
       sr.match_status, sr.list_version_id, sr.screened_at
FROM filing_transactions ft
JOIN payments_b2b p ON p.payment_id = ft.payment_id  -- via ETL copy or federated query in warehouse only
JOIN screening_results sr ON sr.payment_id = p.payment_id
WHERE ft.filing_id = :filingId;

Warehouse Mart (Snowflake — Illustrative)

sql
CREATE TABLE fact_payment_screening AS
SELECT
    p.payment_id,
    p.corporate_id,
    p.amount_usd_equiv,
    s.match_status,
    s.list_version_id,
    w.list_source,
    s.screened_at,
    c.disposition AS case_disposition
FROM stg_payments p
LEFT JOIN stg_screening_results s ON s.payment_id = p.payment_id
LEFT JOIN dim_watchlist_version w ON w.list_version_id = s.list_version_id
LEFT JOIN stg_compliance_cases c ON c.payment_id = p.payment_id;

Async + Human Task

@Transactional("complianceTransactionManager")
public void recordDecision(UUID caseId, CaseDecision decision) {
    ComplianceCase c = caseRepo.findById(caseId).orElseThrow();
    decisionRepo.save(decision.forCase(c));  // INSERT-only table
    c.close(decision.disposition());
    if (decision.releasePayment()) {
        paymentCommandClient.releaseComplianceHold(c.getPaymentId());
    }
}

Part 18 — Common Mistakes

Mistake 1: Compliance DB Updates Payment Row

text
Direct SQL bypass — audit fail — use command API only

Mistake 2: No list_version_id on Screening

text
Cannot prove which OFAC list applied — regulatory finding

Mistake 3: STR Totals from OpenSearch

text
Missing payments — use warehouse mart reconciled to Postgres

Mistake 4: Screening Vendor Response in Payment Table

text
PII leak to payment API — segregate raw_response_ref

Mistake 5: DELETE Case on False Positive

text
Disposition FALSE_POSITIVE — case CLOSED — rows remain

Mistake 6: Sync Vendor on Every Retail Payment

text
Vendor rate limit + capture latency — tiered async

Mistake 7: Watchlist Only in ES

text
No checksum/version in PG — cannot prove ingestion integrity

Mistake 8: Compliance Team Shared Prod DB Credentials

text
Segregation of duties violation — separate roles/services

Part 19 — Interview Questions

Junior

Q1: Compliance vs ledger SoR?

Ledger Postgres owns money; compliance owns screening/cases — links via payment_id.

Q2: STR/SAR purpose?

Report suspicious activity to financial intelligence unit — immutable filing.

Q3: Why watchlist version on screening row?

Prove which sanctions list was active at screen time.

Q4: Async screening impact on capture?

Zero capture latency — flag/hold after if policy requires.

Q5: Can compliance UPDATE account balance?

No — payment/ledger service only.

Mid-Level

Q6: Design screening pipeline for PayFlow retail.

Outbox Kafka consumer, screening_results, optional case, command API hold, idempotent, list_version.

Q7: B2B pre-debit vs retail post-capture?

Risk-based — high value sync hold before ledger — retail async.

Q8: STR filing data sources?

Warehouse mart reconciled to Postgres — case decisions — S3 WORM package — not ES alone.

Q9: False positive handling data model?

case_decisions INSERT FALSE_POSITIVE — screening_results retained — rescreen new row if list updates.

Q10: OpenSearch role in compliance?

Analyst case/note search — not payment SoR or regulatory totals.

Senior

Q11: Architecture diagram compliance platform linked to CorpPay.

compliance_db, watchlist ingestion, Kafka, payment command API, Snowflake marts, S3 filings, RBAC split.

Q12: OFAC emergency rescreen batch design.

New list_version, batch job payment_ids 24h, new screening_results, reopen cases policy, monitor lag.

Q13: Reconciliation between screening coverage and payments.

Nightly: payments without screening_result > SLA — alert Tier 1.

Staff / Architect

Q14: Regulator exam data architecture narrative.

Tier map, immutability, segregation, sample payment trace payment_id across stores with roles.

Q15: GDPR + sanctions — conflicting retention?

Legal hold overrides — jurisdiction table — PII minimization tokenized beneficiary_token.

Scenario

Scenario: "Analyst cleared case but payment still held."

releaseComplianceHold command failed — check outbox/saga — case CLOSED but payment status stuck — reconciliation job payment vs case disposition.

Final synthesis of Lessons 1–59 · The Solution Architect playbook for interviews, design reviews, and production

Part 1 — Concept

What Is Event-Driven Data Architecture?

Event-driven data architecture is how database state changes propagate to other services, read models, analytics, and compliance systems through reliable events — without sacrificing local ACID on the write path or falling into distributed transaction traps.

text
WRITE PATH (strong, local)              EVENT PATH (async, eventual)
──────────────────────────              ─────────────────────────────
@Transactional Postgres                 Kafka / message bus
  business row + outbox (L37)    ──►      consumers: ledger, read model,
  OR WAL captured by CDC (L51)            compliance, Cassandra, ES, warehouse

The Integration Patterns You Must Master

PatternLessonOne line
Local ACIDL33One database, one commit
Transactional outboxL37Business row + event intent same txn
Saga + compensationL38Cross-service workflow without 2PC
CDC (Debezium)L51DB log → stream — row-level
CQRS / read modelL50Write schema ≠ query schema
IdempotencyL43, L53At-least-once safe consumers
ObservabilityL55, L57trace_id in logs → ES correlation

Solution Architect Playbook (This Lesson)

text
1. Classify data (Tier 0–3) — L56
2. Choose write pattern (local txn only)
3. Choose fan-out (outbox vs CDC vs both)
4. Choose read path (replica / read model / search)
5. Define consistency catalog per API
6. Mandate reconciliation + DR evidence
7. Draw failure degradation matrix

Part 2 — History

How Payment Platforms Integrated Data (1990s → Today)

text
1990s   Shared Oracle + 2PC between modules — tight coupling — ops pain
2000s   ESB + JMS — still fragile dual-write to DB and queue
2010s   Microservices ban 2PC — outbox pattern documented widely
2015+   Kafka standard — saga choreography vs orchestration debates
2018    Debezium CDC mature — hybrid outbox (domain) + CDC (analytics)
2020+   PayFlow/CorpPay-style polyglot (L57–59) — one platform event bus
        OpenTelemetry trace_id mandatory — ES for ops not SoR
2024+   Architect interview = draw tiers + event flows + failure modes
        Not "what is Kafka" — but **when outbox vs CDC vs saga step**

Final Historical Lesson

The industry did not replace databases with events. It connected databases with events while keeping money in PostgreSQL.

Part 3 — Problem Statement

What Problem Does Event-Driven Integration Solve?

Problem 1: Dual Write

text
COMMIT payment ✓ · publish Kafka ✗ → ledger never debited
Outbox fixes: both in one txn — relay publishes later

Problem 2: Cross-Service Workflow

text
Payment captured · ledger debit · notify · compliance screen — no global XA
Saga: local txns + compensations + idempotent consumers

Problem 3: Read/Analytics Without Hurting OLTP

text
Projectors build read models · CDC feeds warehouse · OLTP untouched

Problem 4: Observable Incidents

text
Payment failed — trace_id spans payment, ledger, compliance logs in ES
Postgres confirms status — ES explains why

Problem 5: Architect Communication

text
Product asks "real-time everywhere" — catalog defines strong vs eventual per API

Part 4 — Why This Exists

They Are Complementary, Not Competing

text
OUTBOX     → business semantics (PaymentCaptured, ComplianceHold)
CDC        → mirror/analytics (all column changes to Snowflake)
SAGA       → multi-step cross-shard/cross-service consistency
CQRS       → query performance decoupling
IDEMPOTENCY→ at-least-once reality of Kafka
RECONCILE  → eventual consistency becomes auditable

Removing any one in Tier 0 banking creates a known failure class (Lesson 56 anti-patterns).

Part 5 — Internal Working

Reference Event Flow — Unified Model

text

Outbox Relay Internals

text
Loop (or separate relay service per shard):
  SELECT * FROM outbox_events
  WHERE published_at IS NULL
  ORDER BY created_at
  LIMIT 500 FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED;

  FOR each row:
    kafka.send(topic, key=aggregate_id, value=payload, headers=event_id)
    UPDATE outbox_events SET published_at = NOW()

Batch + jdbc batch_size (L47) — monitor unpublished backlog
Alternative: CDC outbox table only — Debezium as relay (L51)

Saga Orchestration Internals (P2P Cross-Shard — L57)

text
Orchestrator state: saga_instances (payment-service or dedicated saga-svc)

Step 1: debitSender(shard A)
  local @Transactional → ledger_entries + account UPDATE + outbox P2PDebited
  on fail → abort saga FAILED

Step 2: creditReceiver(shard B)
  on fail → compensate: creditBackSender (idempotent saga_step_id)
  on success → saga COMPLETED

Each step consumer: processed_events(event_id) OR saga_step_id UNIQUE

CDC Parallel Path (Analytics — L51)

text
Debezium: payments, ledger_entries, screening_results → Kafka
Snowflake sink: fact_payments, fact_ledger, fact_screening
Does NOT replace outbox for PaymentCaptured semantics if payload enrichment needed
Hybrid: outbox for workflow · CDC for warehouse mirror

Part 8 — Execution Flow

Pattern Selection Flows

Flow A — Domain Event Needed (Default)

text
Use OUTBOX when:
  ✓ Downstream needs business meaning (PaymentCaptured, ComplianceReleased)
  ✓ Enriched payload not identical to row
  ✓ Saga / compliance / notification orchestration
Implementation: same @Transactional as payment (L37)

Flow B — Analytics Mirror

text
Use CDC when:
  ✓ Warehouse needs all column changes
  ✓ Many tables, many consumers — platform team operates Debezium
  ✓ Search index mirror 1:1 row (optional — ES projector often better)
Implementation: Debezium + Schema Registry + idempotent sink

Flow C — Cross-Shard P2P

text
Use SAGA when:
  ✓ Two Postgres shards — no XA (L39, L44)
Implementation: orchestrator + compensate + idempotent steps
Never: @Transactional spanning two DataSources

Flow D — Customer List UI

text
Use CQRS READ MODEL when:
  ✓ JOIN/load would hit OLTP (L48, L50)
Implementation: Kafka consumer UPSERT payment_list_view + reconciliation
Consistency: eventual 5s SLA in catalog

Flow E — Incident Investigation

text
Use OBSERVABILITY when:
  ✓ Ops needs trace across services (L55, L57)
Implementation: structured logs trace_id → ES — Postgres for final status
Never: ES balance or STR totals (L59)

Part 11 — Code / SQL Examples

Platform Integration Reference Code

Outbox + Capture (Canonical)

java
@Transactional
public PaymentResult capture(CaptureCommand cmd) {
    idempotencyService.assertFirstOrReplay(cmd);

    Payment payment = paymentRepo.save(Payment.pending(cmd));
    outboxRepo.save(OutboxEvent.builder()
        .eventId(UUID.randomUUID())
        .eventType("PaymentCreated")
        .aggregateId(payment.getPaymentId().toString())
        .payload(toJson(PaymentCreatedEvent.from(payment)))
        .build());

    return PaymentResult.from(payment);
}

Idempotent Consumer Template

java
@KafkaListener(topics = "payment-events")
@Transactional
public void onEvent(PaymentEventEnvelope env) {
    if (processedEventRepo.existsById(env.eventId())) return;

    switch (env.eventType()) {
        case "PaymentCreated" -> ledgerService.debit(env.payload());
        case "PaymentReversed" -> ledgerService.compensate(env.payload());
        default -> log.warn("Unknown {}", env.eventType());
    }
    processedEventRepo.save(new ProcessedEvent(env.eventId()));
}

Saga Compensation Sketch

java
public void compensateDebit(UUID sagaId, P2PCommand cmd) {
    if (sagaStepRepo.existsBySagaIdAndStep(sagaId, "COMPENSATE_DEBIT")) return;
    shardRouter.runOnShard(cmd.senderCustomerId(), () -> {
        ledgerService.creditBack(cmd, sagaId);
        sagaStepRepo.markDone(sagaId, "COMPENSATE_DEBIT");
    });
}

Reconciliation Job (Platform Mandatory)

sql
-- Unpublished outbox > 5 min
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM outbox_events
WHERE published_at IS NULL AND created_at < NOW() - INTERVAL '5 minutes';

-- Consumer lag proxy: payments without ledger entry
SELECT p.payment_id
FROM payments p
LEFT JOIN ledger_entries le ON le.payment_id = p.payment_id AND le.entry_type = 'PAYMENT_DEBIT'
WHERE p.status = 'CAPTURED'
  AND p.created_at >= NOW() - INTERVAL '1 hour'
  AND le.entry_id IS NULL;

Structured Log (Observability)

java
log.info("payment_capture_completed paymentId={} correlationId={} shardId={} status={}",
    payment.getPaymentId(), payment.getCorrelationId(), shardId, payment.getStatus());
// MDC: trace_id, correlation_id → ES

Part 14 — Hibernate/JPA Integration

JPA in Event-Driven Architecture

Do

text
✅ Short @Transactional capture + outbox persist
✅ Persistable UUID (L46) — persist not merge on capture
✅ @Version on contested aggregates
✅ @Modifying bulk mark outbox published (relay)
✅ DTO projection for read APIs (L48)
✅ AFTER_COMMIT listener for non-critical Mongo enrich (L52)

Don't

text
❌ @PostPersist → Kafka (dual write without outbox row ordering guarantee)
❌ Lazy load in Kafka consumer without fetch plan
❌ @Transactional spanning Kafka send
❌ Entity returned from REST
❌ Long @Transactional saga waiting on HTTP

Consumer JPA vs JDBC

text
High-volume projector: JdbcTemplate UPSERT (L50, L51)
Low-volume ledger saga: JPA acceptable with clear aggregates
Outbox relay mark published: native @Modifying + clearAutomatically

Part 19 — Interview Questions

Junior

Q1: Outbox pattern purpose?

Atomic business write + event row; relay publishes to Kafka reliably.

Q2: Why not 2PC in microservices?

Blocking, fragile, poor fit — use saga + outbox (L39).

Q3: At-least-once meaning?

Duplicates possible — consumers must be idempotent.

Q4: CDC vs outbox?

CDC: log row changes. Outbox: domain events. Hybrid common.

Q5: trace_id purpose?

Correlate logs across services in ES during incidents.

Mid-Level

Q6: Design payment capture integration.

Redis NX + PG txn payment+outbox + relay + idempotent ledger consumer + reconciliation.

Q7: Read model lag acceptable where?

List UI yes with SLA; balance and capture response no.

Q8: Consumer failure handling?

Retry, DLT, processed_events idempotency, saga compensate if partial.

Q9: Schema change with Kafka events?

eventVersion, additive fields, deploy consumers first.

Q10: Compliance hold without ledger access?

Command API to payment-service — events ComplianceHold (L59).

Senior

Q11: Draw PayFlow architecture from memory.

8 shards, outbox, saga P2P, read model, Redis, ES, reconcile, DR (L57+L60).

Q12: Kafka down 2 hours — what happens?

Outbox accumulates; capture continues until backlog ADR threshold; lag on ledger/read; recovery replay; no duplicate if idempotent.

Q13: Outbox relay vs Debezium on outbox table?

App relay: simple control. Debezium: platform standardized, slot ops.

Staff / Solution Architect

Q14: Build vs buy event platform for bank?

Managed Kafka + Debezium ops vs self-run; ADR criteria team size, regulators, cost.

Q15: 60-second architecture pitch Lessons 1–59.

Postgres money strong; outbox/saga integrate; CQRS/CDC read/analytics; Redis coord; polyglot tiered; reconcile+DR; compliance separate boundary.

Scenario

Scenario: "Stakeholder wants Elasticsearch as payment system of record for faster search."

Reject — ES investigation tier; Postgres SoR; read model or ES projection with disclaimer; ADR reference L55–L56.
